### AuthorizationModule

File: `src/issuer/issuance/oid4vci/authorization/authorization.module.ts`
providers: `AuthorizationServersService`, `AuthorizeService`, `ChainedAsService`, `ChainedAsVpService`, `InteractiveAuthorizationService`
imports: `ConfigurationModule`, `CryptoModule`, `Oid4vpModule`, `PresentationsModule`, `SessionModule`, `TrustModule`
exports: `AuthorizationServersService`, `AuthorizeService`, `ChainedAsService`, `ChainedAsVpService`, `InteractiveAuthorizationService`

Description: Authorization Module - Groups the OID4VCI authorization server implementations. Bundles the four authorization-server variants and their shared logic: authorize — the issuer-native OAuth 2.0 / OID4VCI authorization server (authorization code, pre-authorized code, refresh token, interactive auth). authorization-servers — managed OID4VP-backed authorization servers. chained-as — chained authorization server delegating to an upstream OIDC provider. chained-as-vp — chained authorization server backed by an OID4VP presentation flow. The authorization-server services are exported so the surrounding issuance components (e.g. metadata and well-known endpoints) can consume them.

exports: `DataEncryptionService`

Description: Global module that provides encryption services for data at rest. This module initializes the encryption transformer on startup. Key source is configured via ENCRYPTION\_KEY\_SOURCE environment variable: "env" (default): Derive key from MASTER\_SECRET (development only) "vault": Fetch from HashiCorp Vault at runtime (production) "aws": Fetch from AWS Secrets Manager at runtime (production) "azure": Fetch from Azure Key Vault at runtime (production)

### AccessCertificateService

File: `src/registrar/access-certificate.service.ts`

Description: Handles creation of access certificates via the registrar API and their subsequent storage in the local certificate store.

Methods:

AUDIT\_LOG\_MAX\_ENTRIES\_PER\_TENANT — keep only the last N entries per tenant (0 = disabled). Runs daily at 03:00.

### AuthorizeService

File: `src/issuer/issuance/oid4vci/authorization/authorize/authorize.service.ts`

Properties:
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(AuthorizeService.name)`

Methods:
- `authzMetadata(tenantId: string): Promise<AuthorizationServerMetadata>`
- `buildAuthorizationDetailsForToken(session: { auth_queries?: AuthorizeQueries; credentialPayload?: any }): [] | undefined` — Build the RFC 9396 authorization\_details array that must be bound to the issued access token, per OID4VCI Section 6 / 7. The list of authorized credential\_configuration\_id values is derived from the session: If the Wallet sent authorization\_details in the Authorization / PAR request (Authorization Code Flow), those values are used. Otherwise (Pre-Authorized Code Flow or issuer-initiated offer), the credential\_configuration\_ids from the Credential Offer are used. Returns undefined when no credential bindings can be derived, in which case no authorization\_details will be placed on the token.
- `challengeRequest(tenantId: string): Promise<{ attestation_challenge: string }>` — Client Attestation Challenge Endpoint. Generates and stores a nonce for use in the Client Attestation PoP JWT. See OAuth2-ATCA07-8
- `describeMalformedTokenRequest(body: unknown): string`
- `extractTokenErrorDescription(error: unknown): string | undefined`
- `getAuthorizationServer(tenantId: string, sessionId?: string): Oauth2AuthorizationServer`
- `getAuthzIssuer(tenantId: string): string`
- `handlePar(tenantId: string, body: AuthorizeQueries, clientAttestation?: { clientAttestationJwt: string; clientAttestationPopJwt: string }): Promise<{ expires_in: number; request_uri: string }>` — Handle a Pushed Authorization Request (PAR). Validates client attestation if provided/required, creates a session, and returns a request\_uri for the authorize endpoint.
- `mapToTokenErrorCode(errorCode: string | undefined): "invalid_request" | "invalid_client" | "invalid_grant" | "invalid_tx_code"` — Map error codes from the OAuth library to OAuth 2.0 Token Error codes. According to OID4VCI Section 6.3: invalid\_request: Transaction code provided but not expected, or expected but not provided invalid\_tx\_code: Wrong transaction code in the Pre-Authorized Code Flow invalid\_grant: Wrong pre-authorized code, or expired code invalid\_client: Anonymous access with pre-authorized code but not supported
- `resolveRefreshTokenConfig(issuanceConfig: { authorizationServers?: Array | null }): { enabled: boolean; expiresInSeconds?: number }`
- `sendAuthorizationResponse(values: AuthorizeQueries, tenantId: string): any`
- `setAuthCode(issuer_state: string): unknown` — Set the authorization code for a session based on the issuer\_state and return the code.
- `validateTokenRequest(body: any, req: Request, tenantId: string): Promise<any>` — Validate the token request. This endpoint is used to exchange the authorization code for an access token. Returns errors according to OID4VCI Section 6.3 Token Error Response.

### AwsSecretsManagerEncryptionKeyProvider

File: `src/platform/data-encryption/providers/aws-secrets-manager-encryption-key.provider.ts`

Description: AWS Secrets Manager encryption key provider. Fetches the encryption key from AWS Secrets Manager at startup. Security benefits: Key is fetched at runtime, only exists in RAM Not exposed via environment variables AWS provides IAM-based access control, audit logging via CloudTrail Automatic key rotation support via AWS Secrets Manager rotation Works seamlessly with IAM roles for EKS/ECS (no credentials in env vars) Required environment variables: AWS\_REGION: AWS region (e.g., us-east-1) AWS\_ENCRYPTION\_SECRET\_NAME: Secret name in Secrets Manager Optional (if not using IAM roles): AWS\_ACCESS\_KEY\_ID: AWS access key AWS\_SECRET\_ACCESS\_KEY: AWS secret key Secret format in AWS Secrets Manager: Plain text: 32-byte key encoded as base64 or hex JSON: { "key": " " }

Properties:
- `client: SecretsManagerClient`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger( AwsSecretsManagerEncryptionKeyProvider.name, )`
- `name: string = "aws"`
- `secretKey: string`
- `secretName: string`

Methods:
- `fingerprint(key: Buffer): string` — Generate a safe fingerprint of the key for logging (first 8 chars of SHA-256 hash).
- `getKey(): Promise<Buffer>`

### AzureKeyVaultEncryptionKeyProvider

File: `src/platform/data-encryption/providers/azure-keyvault-encryption-key.provider.ts`

Description: Azure Key Vault encryption key provider. Fetches the encryption key from Azure Key Vault at startup. Security benefits: Key is fetched at runtime, only exists in RAM Not exposed via environment variables Azure provides RBAC-based access control, audit logging via Azure Monitor Works seamlessly with Managed Identity (no credentials in env vars) Supports key rotation via Key Vault versioning Required environment variables: AZURE\_KEYVAULT\_URL: Key Vault URL (e.g., https://myvault.vault.azure.net ) AZURE\_ENCRYPTION\_SECRET\_NAME: Secret name in Key Vault Authentication (in order of preference): Managed Identity (when running in Azure) Environment credentials (AZURE\_CLIENT\_ID, AZURE\_TENANT\_ID, AZURE\_CLIENT\_SECRET) Azure CLI credentials (for local development) Secret format in Azure Key Vault: Plain text: 32-byte key encoded as base64 or hex

Properties:
- `client: SecretClient`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger( AzureKeyVaultEncryptionKeyProvider.name, )`
- `name: string = "azure"`
- `secretName: string`

Methods:
- `fingerprint(key: Buffer): string` — Generate a safe fingerprint of the key for logging (first 8 chars of SHA-256 hash).
- `getKey(): Promise<Buffer>`

### CertificateBuilderService

File: `src/crypto/key/cert/certificate-builder.service.ts`

Description: Pure X.509 certificate construction. The certificate signature is produced by the KMS adapter, so private key material never leaves the configured backend (DB, Vault Transit, AWS KMS). The mechanism: we pass a makeKmsSigningKey CryptoKey-shaped marker to @peculiar/x509 . The KmsCryptoProvider (installed globally on x509.cryptoProvider ) intercepts subtle.sign(...) for those keys and routes the call to KmsAdapter.sign.

Methods:
- `createCaSignedCert(opts: { caAdapter: KmsAdapter; caRef: KmsKeyRef; caCertPem: string; subjectPublicJwk: JWK; subjectCN: string; hostname: string; notBefore: Date; notAfter: Date; subje…): Promise<{ cert: string; chain: string[] }>`
- `createSelfSignedCaCert(adapter: KmsAdapter, ref: KmsKeyRef, subjectCN: string, hostname: string, notBefore: Date, notAfter: Date): Promise<string>`
- `createSelfSignedCert(adapter: KmsAdapter, ref: KmsKeyRef, subjectCN: string, hostname: string, notBefore: Date, notAfter: Date): Promise<string>`
- `generateSerialNumber(): string`
- `splitPemChain(pem: string): string[]`

### CertService

File: `src/crypto/key/cert/cert.service.ts`

Description: Service for managing certificates. In the new unified model, certificates are stored directly in KeyChainEntity (activeCertificate, rootCertificate, previousCertificate). This service provides a compatibility layer for existing consumers.

Properties:
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(CertService.name)`

Methods:
- `addCertificate(tenantId: string, options: { crt: string[]; keyId: string; description?: string }): Promise<string>` — Add an external certificate to an existing key chain. Used for storing certificates obtained from external sources (e.g., registrar).
- `find(options: FindCertOptions): Promise<CertificateInfo>` — Find a certificate by type (usage type). Returns the certificate from the matching key chain.
- `findOrCreate(options: FindCertOptions): Promise<CertificateInfo>` — Find or create a certificate for a key chain. In the new model, certificates are always created with the key chain, so this just returns the existing one.
- `getCertChain(cert: CertificateInfo): string[]` — Get the certificate chain as an array of base64-encoded DER certificates. Used for the x5c header in JWTs. Per JOSE/x5c usage, trust anchors must not be included in the presented chain. If a root certificate is configured on the key chain and appears as the trailing certificate in the active chain, it is removed.
- `getCertHash(cert: CertificateInfo): string` — Compute the SHA-256 hash of the leaf certificate (for x509\_hash client\_id). Returns the hash as a base64url-encoded string.
- `getCertificateById(tenantId: string, certId: string): Promise<CertificateInfo>` — Get a certificate by ID (key chain ID).
- `getHostname(): string` — Get the hostname from the PUBLIC\_URL config.
- `getLeafCertBase64(cert: CertificateInfo): string[]` — Get only the leaf (signing) certificate as a base64-encoded DER certificate array. Used for x5c headers where only the signing certificate should be included (e.g., status lists).
- `parseCertificateChain(pemChain: string): string[]` — Parse a PEM certificate chain into an array of PEM strings.
- `toBase64Der(pem: string): string`
- `validateCertificate(cert: CertificateInfo): Promise<CertValidationResult>` — Validate a certificate for expiry and revocation.

### ChainedAsService

File: `src/issuer/issuance/oid4vci/authorization/chained-as/chained-as.service.ts`

Description: Service implementing Chained Authorization Server functionality. In Chained AS mode, EUDIPLO acts as an OAuth Authorization Server facade: Receives OAuth requests from wallets Delegates user authentication to an upstream OIDC provider Issues its own access tokens containing issuer\_state This enables session correlation without requiring modifications to the upstream OIDC provider (e.g., Keycloak).

Properties:
- `AUTH_CODE_LIFETIME_SECONDS: number = 300` — Default authorization code lifetime in seconds
- `discoveryCache: unknown = new Map< string, { doc: OidcDiscoveryDocument; expiresAt: number } >()` — Cache for upstream OIDC discovery documents
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(ChainedAsService.name)`
- `REQUEST_URI_PREFIX: string = "urn:ietf:params:oauth:request_uri:"` — Request URI prefix for PAR responses
- `SESSION_LIFETIME_SECONDS: number = 600` — Default session lifetime in seconds

Methods:
- `assertFederationTrustForUpstreamIssuer(upstreamIssuer: string, federationTrustSource?: FederationTrustSource): Promise<void>`
- `buildErrorRedirect(redirectUri: string, error: string, errorDescription?: string, walletState?: string): string` — Build error redirect URL for wallet.
- `buildTokenPayload(tenantId: string, session: ChainedAsSessionEntity, tokenLifetime: number, jti: string, dpopJkt?: string): Record<string, unknown>` — Build access token payload.
- `cleanupExpiredSessions(): Promise<number>` — Clean up expired sessions.
- `exchangeUpstreamCode(session: ChainedAsSessionEntity, code: string, config: ChainedAsConfig, discovery: OidcDiscoveryDocument, callbackUrl: string): Promise<void>` — Exchange authorization code with upstream OIDC provider.
- `getChainedAsBaseUrl(tenantId: string): string` — Get the base URL for this tenant's Chained AS.
- `getChainedAsConfig(tenantId: string): Promise<ChainedAsConfig>` — Get the Chained AS configuration for a tenant.
- `getJwks(tenantId: string): Promise<{ keys: Record[] }>` — Get the JWKS for token verification.
- `getMetadata(tenantId: string): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>` — Get authorization server metadata for the Chained AS.
- `getUpstreamDiscovery(tenantId: string, issuer: string): Promise<OidcDiscoveryDocument>` — Fetch the OIDC discovery document from an upstream provider. Results are cached for 5 minutes.
- `getUpstreamIdentityByIssuerState(issuerState: string): Promise<AuthorizationIdentity | undefined>` — Get upstream identity claims by issuer state. Used to retrieve the upstream OIDC provider's claims for webhook calls.
- `handleAuthorize(tenantId: string, clientId: string, requestUri: string): Promise<string>` — Handle the authorize endpoint. Validates the request\_uri and redirects to the upstream OIDC provider.
- `handlePar(tenantId: string, request: ChainedAsParRequestDto, dpopJkt?: string, clientAttestation?: { clientAttestationJwt: string; clientAttestationPopJwt: string }): Promise<ChainedAsParResponseDto>` — Handle a Pushed Authorization Request (PAR). Creates a session and returns a request\_uri for the authorize endpoint.
- `handleToken(tenantId: string, request: ChainedAsTokenRequestDto, dpopJwt?: string): Promise<ChainedAsTokenResponseDto>` — Handle the token endpoint. Exchanges the authorization code for an access token.
- `handleUpstreamCallback(tenantId: string, code: string, state: string, error?: string, errorDescription?: string): Promise<string>` — Handle the callback from the upstream OIDC provider. Exchanges the code for tokens and redirects back to the wallet.
- `handleUpstreamError(tenantId: string, state: string, error: string, errorDescription?: string): Promise<string>` — Handle upstream OIDC error in callback.

### ChainedAsVpService

File: `src/issuer/issuance/oid4vci/authorization/chained-as-vp/chained-as-vp.service.ts`

Properties:
- `AUTH_CODE_LIFETIME_SECONDS: number = 300`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(ChainedAsVpService.name)`

### ConfigImportOrchestratorService

File: `src/platform/config-import/config-import-orchestrator.service.ts`

Description: Centralized orchestrator for configuration imports. Imports are processed tenant-by-tenant to provide better log clarity and isolation - if one tenant fails, others can still be imported. Flow: Discover all tenant folders For each tenant: a. Setup tenant (create if needed) b. Run all import phases in order (CORE → CONFIGURATION → REFERENCES → FINAL) Continue with next tenant even if current tenant fails Services should register their import functions during construction. The orchestrator automatically runs imports during onApplicationBootstrap.

Properties:
- `hasRun: unknown = false`
- `importers: RegisteredImporter[] = []`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(ConfigImportOrchestratorService.name)`
- `runPromise: Promise<void> | null = null`
- `tenantSetup: TenantSetupFn | null = null`

Methods:
- `discoverTenants(): string[]` — Discover all tenant folders in the config directory.
- `executeImports(): Promise<void>`
- `onApplicationBootstrap(): any` — Lifecycle hook - automatically triggers import orchestration.
- `register(name: string, phase: ImportPhase, importFn: TenantImportFn): void` — Register an import function for orchestration.
- `registerTenantSetup(name: string, setupFn: function): void` — Register a tenant setup function. This is called first for each tenant to ensure the tenant exists.
- `runImports(): Promise<void>` — Execute all registered imports tenant-by-tenant. Safe to call multiple times - only runs once. Returns the same promise if called while running.

### CredentialChainValidationService

File: `src/verifier/presentations/credential/credential-chain-validation.service.ts`

Description: Shared service for certificate chain validation. Used by both mDOC and SD-JWT-VC verifiers to ensure consistent behavior. Responsibilities: X.509 certificate chain building and validation Trust anchor matching against LoTE trust lists Status list (revocation) verification Detailed error reporting

Methods:
- `buildChainErrorDetails(presented: x509.X509Certificate[], store: BuiltTrustStore, trustListSource: TrustListSource | undefined, error: any): Promise<string>` — Build detailed error information when chain building fails.
- `buildNoMatchErrorDetails(path: x509.X509Certificate[], store: BuiltTrustStore, trustListSource: TrustListSource | undefined, pinnedMode: string): Promise<string>` — Build detailed error information when no trusted entity matches.
- `extractExtensionKeyId(extension: literal type | undefined): string | undefined`
- `fetchStatusListJwt(uri: string): Promise<string>` — Fetch a status list JWT with caching. Delegates to StatusListVerifierService.
- `getThumbprint(cert: x509.X509Certificate): Promise<string>` — Get hex thumbprint of a certificate.
- `getTrustedCertificateBuffers(trustListSource?: TrustListSource): Promise<Uint8Array[]>` — Get trusted certificate buffers for mDOC verification. Returns certificates as Uint8Array\[\] for the mdoc library.
- `getTrustedStatusCertificateBuffers(trustListSource?: TrustListSource): Promise<Uint8Array[]>` — Get trusted revocation certificate buffers for mDOC status validation. Returns certificates as Uint8Array\[\] for the mdoc library.
- `getTrustStoreForAugmentation(trustListSource?: TrustListSource): Promise<BuiltTrustStore | null>` — Best-effort trust store load for NON-authoritative anchor augmentation (supplying extra certificates to the mDOC signature check). Unlike getTrustStoreIfConfigured, an unavailable/stale trust list is swallowed to null here: the authoritative trust decision is made by validateChain, which fails closed on TrustListUnavailableError. Returning no extra anchors from this path is therefore safe.
- `getTrustStoreIfConfigured(trustListSource?: TrustListSource): Promise<BuiltTrustStore | null>`
- `logChainKeyIdentifiers(path: x509.X509Certificate[], anchors: x509.X509Certificate[]): Promise<void>`
- `summarizeTrustedCerts(entities: TrustedEntity[]): Promise<string>` — Summarize trusted entities for error logging.
- `validateChain(x5c: string[], trustListSource: TrustListSource | undefined, policy: ChainValidationPolicy = {}): Promise<ChainValidationResult>` — Validate a certificate chain against the trust store.
- `verifyStatusListSignature(x5c: string[] | undefined, matchedEntity: MatchedTrustedEntity | null, trustListSource: TrustListSource | undefined, policy: ChainValidationPolicy = {}): Promise<boolean>` — Verify a status list JWT signature against the matched entity's revocation certificate.

### CrlValidationService

File: `src/crypto/key/cert/crl-validation.service.ts`

Description: Service for validating certificates against Certificate Revocation Lists (CRL). This service: Extracts CRL Distribution Points from certificates Fetches and caches CRL data Checks if certificates are revoked

Properties:
- `certValidationCache: unknown = new Map< string, { result: CrlValidationResult; timestamp: number } >()` — Short-lived cache for certificate validation results. Prevents repeated validation of the same certificate within a request. Key is the certificate fingerprint, value is the result and timestamp.
- `certValidationCacheTtlMs: unknown = 30 * 1000` — Cache TTL for certificate validation results (30 seconds)
- `crlCache: unknown = new Map<string, CachedCrl>()`
- `defaultCacheTtlMs: unknown = 60 * 60 * 1000` — Default cache TTL in milliseconds (1 hour)
- `fetchTimeoutMs: number = 10000` — Timeout for CRL fetch in milliseconds
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(CrlValidationService.name)`

Methods:
- `arrayBufferToHex(buffer: ArrayBuffer): string` — Convert ArrayBuffer to hex string.
- `checkAgainstCrl(cert: x509.X509Certificate, crlUrl: string): Promise<CrlValidationResult>` — Check a certificate against a specific CRL URL.
- `checkCertificateRevocation(certPem: string): Promise<CrlValidationResult>` — Check if a certificate is revoked according to its CRL.
- `clearCache(): void` — Clear the CRL cache.
- `extractCrlDistributionPoints(cert: x509.X509Certificate): string[]` — Extract CRL Distribution Point URLs from a certificate.
- `extractUrlsFromParsedCdp(value: any, urls: string[]): void` — Extract URLs from parsed CDP extension data.
- `extractUrlsFromRawCdp(rawData: ArrayBuffer, urls: string[]): void` — Extract URLs from raw ASN.1 CDP extension data. This is a fallback when the library doesn't parse it for us.
- `fetchCrl(url: string): Promise<CertificateList>` — Fetch and parse a CRL from a URL, with caching.
- `getCacheStats(): { size: number; urls: string[] }` — Get cache statistics.
- `isCacheValid(cached: CachedCrl): boolean` — Check if a cached CRL is still valid.
- `parseReasonCode(buffer: ArrayBuffer): string` — Parse CRL reason code.

### DataEncryptionService

File: `src/platform/data-encryption/data-encryption.service.ts`

Description: Service for encrypting and decrypting sensitive data at rest. Uses AES-256-GCM for authenticated encryption. The encryption key is fetched at runtime from the configured provider: env: Derived from MASTER\_SECRET (development only) vault: Fetched from HashiCorp Vault (production) aws: Fetched from AWS Secrets Manager (production) azure: Fetched from Azure Key Vault (production) Security: When using vault/aws/azure, the key is only in RAM, not exposed via environment variables.

Properties:
- `algorithm: unknown = "aes-256-gcm" as const`
- `authTagLength: number = 16`
- `encryptionKey: Buffer | null = null`
- `initialized: unknown = false`
- `ivLength: number = 12`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(DataEncryptionService.name)`

Methods:
- `decrypt(encryptedValue: string): string` — Decrypt a value that was encrypted with encrypt(). Expects format: base64(iv):base64(authTag):base64(ciphertext)
- `decryptJson(encryptedValue: string): T` — Decrypt a JSON value.
- `encrypt(plaintext: string): string` — Encrypt a string value using AES-256-GCM. Returns format: base64(iv):base64(authTag):base64(ciphertext)
- `encryptJson(value: T): string` — Encrypt a JSON-serializable value.
- `ensureInitialized(): Buffer` — Ensure the service is initialized before operations.
- `initialize(): Promise<void>` — Initialize the encryption service by fetching the key from the provider. Must be called during module initialization before any encrypt/decrypt operations.
- `isEncrypted(value: string): boolean` — Check if a value appears to be encrypted (has the expected format).

### InteractiveAuthorizationService

File: `src/issuer/issuance/oid4vci/authorization/authorize/interactive-authorization.service.ts`

Description: Service for handling Interactive Authorization Endpoint (IAE) operations. The IAE enables a presentation flow during credential issuance, allowing the issuer to request verifiable presentations from the wallet before issuing credentials. Supports two interaction types: openid4vp\_presentation: Requests a verifiable presentation via OpenID4VP redirect\_to\_web: Redirects to a web-based authorization flow

Properties:
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(InteractiveAuthorizationService.name)`

Methods:
- `advanceOrComplete(authSession: InteractiveAuthSessionEntity, context: ReturnType<(authSession: InteractiveAuthSessionEntity) => { iaeActions: IaeAction[] | undefined; completedStepsData: any[]; supportedTypes: InteractionType[]; }…, tenantId: string, origin: string): Promise<InteractiveAuthorizationResponse>` — Advance to next IAE action or complete the flow.
- `completeWebAuthorization(authSession: string, tenantId: string): Promise<boolean>` — Mark a web authorization as completed. Called when user completes web-based authorization.
- `createErrorResponse(error: string, errorDescription?: string): InteractiveAuthorizationResponse` — Create an error response.
- `createOpenid4vpInteractionResponse(authSession: string, tenantId: string, origin: string, authorizationDetails?: any[]): Promise<InteractiveAuthorizationResponse>` — Create an OpenID4VP interaction response. Generates a presentation request for the wallet. The presentation configuration is determined by: Looking up the credential\_configuration\_id from authorization\_details Using the first iaeAction of type openid4vp\_presentation from that credential config Falling back to the first available presentation configuration
- `createOpenid4vpInteractionResponseForConfig(authSession: string, tenantId: string, origin: string, presentationConfigId: string, label?: string): Promise<InteractiveAuthorizationResponse>` — Create an OpenID4VP interaction response for a specific presentation config.
- `createRedirectToWebResponse(authSession: string, tenantId: string): InteractiveAuthorizationResponse` — Create a redirect\_to\_web interaction response. Generates a PAR request URI for web-based authorization.
- `createRedirectToWebResponseForUrl(authSession: string, tenantId: string, url?: string, description?: string): InteractiveAuthorizationResponse` — Create a redirect\_to\_web interaction response for a specific URL.
- `executeIaeAction(authSession: string, tenantId: string, origin: string, action: IaeAction, supportedTypes: InteractionType[]): Promise<InteractiveAuthorizationResponse>` — Execute a specific IAE action.
- `getAuthorizationServerMetadata(tenantId: string): AuthorizationServerMetadata` — Get the authorization server metadata for interactive authorization.
- `handleCodeVerifier(codeVerifier: string, authSession: InteractiveAuthSessionEntity): Promise<literal type | InteractiveAuthorizationResponse>` — Handle PKCE code\_verifier for redirect\_to\_web flow. Validates the code\_verifier and returns success or error.
- `handleFollowUpRequest(request: InteractiveAuthFollowUpRequest, tenantId: string, origin: string): Promise<InteractiveAuthorizationResponse>` — Handle a follow-up interactive authorization request. Validates the submitted interaction response and either: Advances to the next IAE action, or Issues an authorization code if all steps are complete.
- `handleInitialRequest(request: InteractiveAuthInitialRequest, tenantId: string, origin: string, dpop?: { jwk: Jwk; jwt: string }, clientAttestation?: { clientAttestationJwt: string; clientAttestationPopJwt: string }): Promise<InteractiveAuthorizationResponse>` — Handle an initial interactive authorization request. Creates an auth session and returns the appropriate interaction response. If the credential config has iaeActions defined, those are used. Otherwise, falls back to the default behavior based on wallet-supported types.
- `handleOpenid4vpResponse(openid4vpResponse: string, authSession: InteractiveAuthSessionEntity): Promise<literal type | InteractiveAuthorizationResponse>` — Handle OpenID4VP response from wallet. Validates and stores the VP data, returns success or error.
- `handleRequest(body: InteractiveAuthorizationRequestDto, req: Request, tenantId: string, origin: string): Promise<InteractiveAuthorizationResponse>` — Handle an interactive authorization request. Routes to the appropriate handler based on request type.
- `issueAuthorizationCode(authSession: InteractiveAuthSessionEntity): Promise<InteractiveAuthorizationResponse>` — Issue an authorization code after successful interaction.
- `parseAuthorizationDetails(authDetails: any): [] | undefined` — Parse authorization\_details which can be a string or array.
- `parseRequest(body: InteractiveAuthorizationRequestDto, req: Request, tenantId: string): ParsedInteractiveAuthorizationRequest` — Parse an interactive authorization request. Determines if the request is an initial or follow-up request.
- `parseSessionContext(authSession: InteractiveAuthSessionEntity): { iaeActions: [] | undefined; completedStepsData: any[]; supportedTypes: InteractionType[] }` — Parse session context data.
- `processCodeVerifierFollow(codeVerifier: string, authSession: InteractiveAuthSessionEntity, context: ReturnType<(authSession: InteractiveAuthSessionEntity) => { iaeActions: IaeAction[] | undefined; completedStepsData: any[]; supportedTypes: InteractionType[]; }…, tenantId: string, origin: string): Promise<InteractiveAuthorizationResponse>` — Process code\_verifier follow-up response.
- `processOpenid4vpFollow(openid4vpResponse: string, authSession: InteractiveAuthSessionEntity, context: ReturnType<(authSession: InteractiveAuthSessionEntity) => { iaeActions: IaeAction[] | undefined; completedStepsData: any[]; supportedTypes: InteractionType[]; }…, tenantId: string, origin: string): Promise<InteractiveAuthorizationResponse>` — Process OpenID4VP follow-up response.
- `validateAuthSession(authSession: string, tenantId: string): Promise<InteractiveAuthSessionEntity | InteractiveAuthorizationResponse>` — Validate and retrieve an auth session.
- `verifyPkce(codeVerifier: string, codeChallenge: string, method?: string): Promise<boolean>` — Verify PKCE code\_verifier against code\_challenge.

### Iso18013Service

File: `src/verifier/iso18013/iso18013.service.ts`

Methods:
- `buildReaderAuthForOffer(tenantId: string, accessKeyChainId: string | undefined, itemsRequest: ItemsRequest, encryptionInfoB64u: string, origin: string): Promise<ReaderAuth>` — Build a detached ReaderAuth (COSE\_Sign1) for the offer, signing the ReaderAuthentication structure with the tenant's Access key chain. The DCAPIHandover SessionTranscript is reconstructed deterministically from the EncryptionInfo (base64url) and browser origin — identical to the one the wallet derives — so the reader signature binds to this exact request. Note: signing extracts the Access private key as a JWK (mirroring mDOC issuance), so KMS-backed non-extractable keys are not yet supported for reader authentication.
- `createOffer(requestId: string, tenantId: string, origin: string, skewSeconds?: number, webhook?: WebhookConfig): Promise<Iso18013Offer>` — Create an ISO 18013-7 Annex C offer: build DeviceRequest + encryptionInfo and persist a session for the response phase.
- `processResponse(sessionId: string, encryptedB64: string): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>` — Process the HPKE-encrypted DeviceResponse returned by the wallet via DC API.
- `resolveWebhookFromEndpoint(webhookEndpointId: string | null | undefined, tenantId: string): Promise<WebhookConfig | undefined>`

For the db provider we keep the full private JWK (so signing can re-import it). For external providers we keep only the public JWK — the private key lives in the KMS backend.

### KeyRotationService

File: `src/crypto/key/key-rotation.service.ts`

Description: Service responsible for automatic key rotation. Key chains with rotationEnabled=true are checked periodically. When lastRotatedAt + rotationIntervalDays has passed, the key is rotated: New key material is generated A new certificate is generated (signed by root CA if internal chain) Previous key is preserved for grace period

Properties:
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(KeyRotationService.name)`

Methods:
- `checkForRotation(): Promise<void>` — Cron job that runs daily to check for keys that need rotation.
- `findKeyChainNeedingRotation(): Promise<KeyChainEntity[]>` — Find all key chains that have rotation enabled and are due for rotation.
- `rotateKeyChain(tenantId: string, keyChainId: string): Promise<void>` — Manually trigger rotation for a specific key chain.

If the token does not carry authorization\_details (e.g. scope-only external AS integrations), the check is skipped. when the requested credential is not authorized by the token.

Fetches the tenant's encryption public key and returns the metadata block advertising that the issuer can receive encrypted credential requests.
- `getDeferredCredential(req: Request, body: DeferredCredentialRequestDto, tenantId: string): Promise<CredentialResponse>` — Handle deferred credential request. Called when wallet polls with transaction\_id.
- `getIssuer(tenantId: string, sessionId?: string): any` — Get the OID4VCI issuer instance for a specific tenant.
- `getResourceServer(tenantId: string, sessionId?: string): any` — Get the OID4VCI resource server instance for a specific tenant.
- `getSelectedAuthorizationServerConfig(tenantId: string, selectedAuthorizationServer?: string): unknown`

- `isJwtActive(jwt: string): boolean`

- `normalizeSchemaMetadataIds(ids: Array<string | null | undefined>): string[]`
- `resolveAuthorizationServerSelection(tenantId: string, selectedAuthorizationServer?: string): Promise<string | undefined>`
- `resolveIssuerRegistrationCertificateJwt(tenantId: string, registrationCertificateConfig: IssuerRegistrationCertificateConfig): Promise<string | undefined>`
- `resolveParsedCredentialProofs(parsedCredentialRequest: ParseCredentialRequestReturn): ParsedCredentialProofs` — Resolve supported key proofs from the parsed credential request. We currently support JWT proof-of-possession and attestation proof types.
- `resolveSessionAndClaims(tokenPayload: OAuth2TokenPayload, tenantId: string, credentialConfigurationId: string, issuanceConfig: Awaited<ReturnType<IssuanceService>>): Promise<{ session: Session; claimsResult: ClaimsWebhookResult | undefined; isExternalAsToken: boolean; isChainedAsToken: boolean }>` — Resolve the session and claims based on the token source. Handles Local AS, Chained AS, and External AS flows.
- `verifyResourceAccessToken(req: Request, tenantId: string, issuerMetadata: IssuerMetadataResult, issuanceConfig: Awaited<ReturnType<IssuanceService>>): Promise<OAuth2TokenPayload>` — Verify the resource access token from the request. Supports both DPoP and Bearer authentication schemes based on configuration.

### Oid4vpService

Returns the cached requestObject if available (for request\_uri\_method="get"), otherwise generates a new one. This ensures the wallet receives the exact same JWT that was stored during session creation, which is essential for transaction\_data hash validation.
- `getResponse(body: AuthorizationResponse, nonce: string): unknown` — Processes the response from the wallet. Per OID4VP spec Section 13.3, the nonce parameter is the walletNonce from the URL path (not the session ID).
- `normalizeExpectedOrigin(origin: string): string | undefined`
- `resolveSessionByNonce(nonce: string): unknown` — Resolves a session from a wallet-facing nonce. Per OID4VP spec Section 13.3, wallet-facing URLs use a separate walletNonce instead of the session ID. Falls back to session ID lookup for backward compatibility with sessions created before the walletNonce migration.

### PresentationsService

File: `src/verifier/presentations/presentations.service.ts`

Description: Service for managing Verifiable Presentations (VPs) and handling SD-JWT-VCs.

Methods:
- `areClaimPathsEqual(left: string[], right: string[]): boolean`
- `buildSchemaMetadataVerifier(signedJwt: string): Promise<SchemaMetadataVerifier>`
- `deletePresentationConfig(id: string, tenantId: string, actorToken?: TokenPayload, req?: Request): unknown` — Deletes a presentation configuration by its ID and tenant ID.
- `deriveSchemaMetadataFormatsFromJwt(signedJwt: string): string[]`
- `extractSkiAsBase64url(derB64: string): string | undefined` — Extract the Subject Key Identifier (SKI, OID 2.5.29.14) from a base64-encoded DER certificate and return it as a base64url string. Wallets check that a credential's certificate chain contains a cert whose AKI matches this SKI, enabling local credential matching without fetching external trust-list resources.
- `getCredentialClaimSelections(credential: CredentialQueryValue): [][]`
- `getOrIssueRegistrationCertificate(presentationConfig: PresentationConfig, resolvedDcqlQuery: any, requestId: string): Promise<string | undefined>` — Resolve the registration-certificate JWT to attach to a VP request, using the embedded PresentationConfig.registrationCertCache when it is still valid. On a cache miss/expiry the cert is freshly resolved via RegistrarService and the cache is persisted. Returns undefined when the config has no registrationCert spec or the registrar is not enabled for this tenant.
- `getPresentationConfig(id: string, tenantId: string): Promise<PresentationConfig>` — Retrieves a presentation configuration by its ID and tenant ID.
- `getPresentationConfigs(tenantId: string): Promise<PresentationConfig[]>` — Retrieves all presentation configurations for a given tenant.
- `getRequiredClaimKeys(claims: ClaimsQuery[] | undefined, credentialType: CredentialType): string[]` — Converts DCQL claim queries to required claim keys for verification. For SD-JWT-VC: paths are joined with dots (e.g., \["address", "locality"\] -\> "address.locality") For mDOC: the first path element is the namespace, so we return the claim name (second element)
- `getType(jwt: string, att: string): CredentialType` — Get the credential type based on the configuration id.
- `hasClaimPath(value: unknown, path: string[]): boolean`
- `importForTenant(tenantId: string): any` — Imports presentation configurations for a specific tenant.
- `listSchemaMetadataCatalog(tenantId: string): unknown` — List schema metadata entries from the connected registrar catalog. Returns an empty array when the registrar is not enabled for the tenant.
- `matchesClaimSelection(payload: Record<string, unknown>, allClaims: ClaimsQuery[] | undefined, selectedClaims: ClaimsQuery[]): boolean`
- `matchesMdocClaimSelection(payload: Record<string, unknown>, selectedClaims: ClaimsQuery[]): boolean`
- `normalizeDcApiOrigin(origin: string | undefined): string | undefined`
- `parseResponse(res: AuthResponse, presentationConfig: PresentationConfig, session: Session): unknown` — Parse the response from the wallet. It will verify the SD-JWT-VCs in the vp\_token and return the parsed attestations.
- `refreshRegistrationCertCache(next: PresentationConfig, existing: PresentationConfig | undefined): Promise<void>` — Recompute (or invalidate) the embedded registration-certificate cache on the about-to-be-saved presentation config. Behavior: If registrationCert is unset → clears any stale cache. If a cache exists for an unchanged registrationCert spec, unchanged dcql\_query , and is not expired → keeps the existing cache. Otherwise eagerly resolves the certificate via RegistrarService and stores the new cache. On registrar/network failure the cache is cleared and the save proceeds; the runtime path will retry. Errors raised by the registrar that indicate user-config problems ( BadRequestException ) propagate to fail the save.
- `refreshRegistrationCertCacheAsync(id: string, tenantId: string): Promise<void>`
- `reissueRegistrationCertificate(id: string, tenantId: string): Promise<PresentationConfig>` — Force-reissue the registration certificate for a presentation config, bypassing the cache. Used by the management UI's "Reissue now" action. Throws if the config has no registrationCert spec or the registrar is not enabled for this tenant.
- `resolveCredentialIssuerMetadata(issuerUrl: string): unknown` — Resolve OID4VCI credential issuer metadata server-side. This is used by the web client to avoid browser CORS restrictions.
- `resolveSchemaMetadata(schemaMetadataUrl: string): Promise<{ signedJwt: string; schema: ResolvedSchemaMetadataPayload }>`
- `resolveSchemaMetadataJwt(signedJwt: string): Promise<{ signedJwt: string; schema: ResolvedSchemaMetadataPayload }>`
- `resolveSdJwtKeyBindingAudience(session: Session, requestObjectSessionData: literal type | undefined): string | undefined`
- `resolveTrustAnchorDer(ref: TrustListRef, tenantId: string): Promise<string | undefined>` — Resolve the base64-encoded DER trust anchor certificate for a TrustListRef. For managed trust lists (trustListId), fetches the verifier certificate from the trust list service. For external refs, uses the supplied verifierX509Der.
- `resolveTrustListRefsForTenant(refs: TrustListRef[] | undefined, tenantId: string, tenantHost: string): Promise<TrustListRef[]>`
- `sanitizePresentationConfigForLog(config: PresentationConfig): Record<string, unknown>`
- `scheduleRegistrationCertRefresh(id: string, tenantId: string): void` — Trigger registration-certificate cache refresh in the background. This keeps create/update endpoints responsive while cert issuance happens asynchronously.
- `storePresentationConfig(tenantId: string, vprequest: PresentationConfigCreateDto, actorToken?: TokenPayload, req?: Request): unknown` — Stores a new presentation configuration.
- `storeRCID(registrationCertId: string, id: string, tenantId: string): any` — Stores the new registration certificate.
- `throwMdocVerificationFailure(attId: string, result: { failureType?: "signature_invalid" | "no_trust_chain_to_root" | "trust_chain_not_trusted" | "x5c_missing" | "verification_error"; failureReason?: string }): never`
- `transformDcqlTrustedAuthoritiesToAki(dcqlQuery: any, tenantId: string): Promise<any>` — Transform trusted\_authorities in a DCQL query from internal etsi\_tl format (TrustListRef objects) to the DCQL-compliant aki format (base64url-encoded Subject Key Identifier strings). Per OID4VP 1.0 Final §6 / trusted-authorities-query, aki values must be an array of strings. This ensures wallets receive a spec-compliant DCQL query rather than the internal representation with TrustListRef objects. For each etsi\_tl entry the Subject Key Identifier (SKI, OID 2.5.29.14) of the trust anchor certificate is extracted and base64url-encoded. The SKI equals the AKI field in any credential signed by that CA, so a wallet can match credentials locally without fetching external resources.
- `updatePresentationConfig(id: string, tenantId: string, vprequest: PresentationConfigUpdateDto, actorToken?: TokenPayload, req?: Request): unknown` — Updates an existing presentation configuration.
- `validateCredentialCompleteness(receivedCredentialIds: string[], requiredCredentials: CredentialQueryValue[], credentialSets?: CredentialSetQuery[]): void` — Validates that the presentation response contains all required credentials. If credential\_sets are defined, validates that at least one option set is fully satisfied. If no credential\_sets are defined, all credentials in the query are required.
- `validateMdocClaims(credentialId: string, requiredClaims: ClaimsQuery[] | undefined, receivedClaims: Record<string, unknown>): void` — Validates that all required claims from the DCQL query are present in the mDOC response.
- `verifyCredentialValue(options: { cred: string; attId: string; type: CredentialType; session: Session; requestObjectSessionData: literal type | undefined; requestObjectJwkThumbprint: Uint8Arra…): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>`
- `verifyMdocCredentialValue(options: { cred: string; attId: string; session: Session; requestObjectSessionData: literal type | undefined; requestObjectJwkThumbprint: Uint8Array | undefined; verifyO…): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>`
- `verifyMdocCredentialWithClaimSets(options: { cred: string; attId: string; sessionData: MdocSessionDataOid4vp | MdocSessionDataDcApi; verifyOptions: VerifierOptions; dcqlCredential: CredentialQueryValue; …): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>`
- `verifySdJwtCredentialValue(options: { cred: string; attId: string; session: Session; requestObjectSessionData: literal type | undefined; requestObjectJwkThumbprint: Uint8Array | undefined; verifyO…): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>`

### RegistrationCertificateService

File: `src/registrar/registration-certificate.service.ts`

Description: Handles registration certificate lifecycle: Resolving (import / lookup / create) registration certificates JWT temporal validation and DCQL authorization checks Stable fingerprint computation used for caching in the VP flow

Properties:
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(RegistrationCertificateService.name)`

Methods:
- `addRegistrationCertificate(req: { id?: string; body?: Partial<RegistrationCertificateCreation>; jwt?: string }, dcqlQuery: any, requestId: string, tenantId: string): Promise<string>` — Resolve a registration certificate and return only the JWT string.
- `canonicalJson(value: any): string` — Recursively canonicalize a JSON value: object keys sorted, arrays preserved in their original order (DCQL arrays are order-significant).
- `computeAuthorizedCredentialsFingerprint(credentials: unknown): string` — Compute a canonical fingerprint over a registration certificate's authorized credentials claim.
- `computeDcqlFingerprint(dcqlQuery: any): string` — Compute a canonical fingerprint over a dcql\_query.credentials array.
- `computeSpecFingerprint(spec: unknown): string` — Compute a stable fingerprint over a registration-certificate spec ( { jwt?, id?, body? } ).
- `dcqlCredentialFingerprint(cred: any): string` — Compute a stable canonical fingerprint of a single credential entry. Normalizes to registrar CredentialDef shape ( format , claims , meta ) before hashing, because DCQL credentials may include transport/query fields that are not present in registrar certificates.
- `hash(input: string): string`
- `resolveRegistrationCertificate(req: { id?: string; body?: Partial<RegistrationCertificateCreation>; jwt?: string }, dcqlQuery: any, requestId: string, tenantId: string): Promise<{ jwt: string; payload: Record<string, any>; source: "imported" | "registrar" }>` — Resolve a registration certificate from a spec ( jwt import / id lookup / body creation), validate it against the effective DCQL query and return both the JWT and its decoded payload. This is the canonical entry point used both at presentation-config save-time (eager caching) and at VP-request time (cache miss / refresh).
- `revokeRegistrationCertificateByJwt(tenantId: string, jwt: string): Promise<boolean>` — Revoke an active registration certificate identified by its JWT. Returns true when a matching active certificate was found and revoked. Returns false when no active matching certificate exists.
- `validateRegistrationCertificate(jwt: string, dcqlQuery: any, tenantId: string, requestId: string, source: "jwt" | "id" | "body"): Record<string, any>` — Validate a registration certificate JWT against the effective DCQL query. Performs: JWT decoding (structural validation). Temporal validity check ( exp , nbf ) with a small clock skew tolerance. DCQL fingerprint comparison: every credential being requested in dcqlQuery.credentials MUST be present in the certificate's authorized credentials claim. Prevents overasking with a cert issued for a different/narrower set of credentials. Fails closed by throwing BadRequestException on any mismatch.

### SdjwtvcverifierService

File: `src/verifier/presentations/credential/sdjwtvcverifier/sdjwtvcverifier.service.ts`

Methods:
- `validateTransactionDataHashes(result: VerificationResult, transactionData: string[]): void` — Validates that the KB-JWT contains transaction\_data\_hashes that match the SHA-256 hashes of the provided transaction data. According to OID4VP spec Appendix B.3.3.1: transaction\_data\_hashes: A non-empty array of strings where each element is a base64url-encoded hash calculated over the transaction data string (base64url decoding is NOT performed before hashing). The hash function defaults to SHA-256 unless transaction\_data\_hashes\_alg specifies otherwise.
- `verify(cred: string, options: VerifierOptions): Promise<VerificationResult>` — Verifies an SD-JWT-VC credential. Creates a fresh SDJwtVcInstance per verification to safely capture the matched TrustedEntity for status list verification. If transaction data is provided in options, this method also validates that the KB-JWT contains matching transaction\_data\_hashes. See OID4VP spec Appendix B.3.3.1 for details.
- `verifyCredential(data: string, signature: string, options: VerifierOptions): Promise<{ verified: boolean; matchedEntity: MatchedTrustedEntity | null }>` — Verifies the SD-JWT-VC credential signature and trust chain. Returns both the verification result and the matched TrustedEntity. data = "\<b64url(header)\>.\<b64url(payload)\>" signature = "\<b64url(signature)\>"
- `verifyKeyBindingJwt(data: string, signature: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>, expectedAudience?: string): Promise<boolean>`
- `verifyStatusList(data: string, signature: string, options: VerifierOptions, matchedEntity: MatchedTrustedEntity | null): Promise<boolean>` — Verifies the status list JWT using the revocation certificate from the same TrustedEntity that issued the credential. This ensures that the status list is signed by the authorized revocation service of the same entity that issued the credential.

### SessionLogStoreService

- `append(sessionId: string, level: SessionLogLevel, message: string, stage?: string, detail?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>` — Append a log entry to the database if the store mode allows it.
- `deleteBySessionId(sessionId: string): Promise<void>` — Delete all log entries for a session.
- `findBySessionId(sessionId: string): Promise<SessionLogEntry[]>` — Retrieve all log entries for a session, ordered by timestamp.

### SessionService

File: `src/session/session.service.ts`

Properties:
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(SessionService.name)`
- `sessionsGauge: UpDownCounter`

Methods:
- `add(issuer_state: string, values: QueryDeepPartialEntity<Session>): any` — Update an existing session.
- `consumeOfferByReference(sessionId: string, tenantId: string): Promise<boolean>` — Consume a credential offer stored on a session by clearing the offer payload only if it is still present. Returns true when the offer was consumed, false when it was already consumed or the session did not match.
- `create(session: DeepPartial<Session>): unknown` — Create a new session.
- `delete(id: string, sub: string): Promise<any>` — Deletes a session by its ID and tenant ID.
- `findByWalletNonce(nonce: string): any` — Find a session by its walletNonce (used in wallet-facing URLs). Returns null if no session matches.
- `get(state: string): any` — Get a session by its state.
- `getAll(tenantId: string, query: SessionQueryDto): Promise<PaginatedSessionResponseDto>` — Get sessions with pagination and optional filtering.
- `getBy(where: FindOptionsWhere<Session>): any` — Get a session by a specific condition.
- `incrementTxCodeFailedAttempts(sessionId: string): Promise<number>` — Atomically increments the failed tx\_code attempt counter for a session. Returns the updated attempt count. Used for brute-force protection in the OID4VCI pre-authorized code flow.
- `onApplicationBootstrap(): unknown` — Register the tidy up cron job on application bootstrap. This will run every hour by default, but can be configured via the SESSION\_TIDY\_UP\_INTERVAL config variable.
- `resolveExternalAuthorizationServerSession(tenantId: string, externalIssuer: string, externalSubject: string, authorizationServerId?: string, bindingClaim?: string, bindingValue?: string): Promise<Session>` — Resolve an existing issuance session for an external authorization-server token. The lookup is intentionally strict: an access token must identify the trusted authorization server and a configured session-correlation claim, and the resulting session must already exist. No implicit "create on miss" behavior.
- `setState(session: Session, status: SessionStatus): any` — Marks the session as successful or failed. Emits a session status change event for SSE subscribers.
- `tidyUpSessions(): any` — Tidy up sessions based on per-tenant configuration. Each tenant can configure their own TTL and cleanup mode. 'full' mode: Deletes the entire session record 'anonymize' mode: Keeps session metadata but removes personal data

### StatusListService

File: `src/issuer/status-list/status-list.service.ts`

Properties:
- `keyChainService: KeyChainService`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(StatusListService.name)`

Methods:
- `buildAggregationUri(tenantId: string): string` — Build the aggregation URI for a tenant. This endpoint returns all status list URIs for the tenant. See RFC draft-ietf-oauth-status-list Section 9.
- `buildStatusListUri(tenantId: string, listId: string): string` — Build the URI for a status list.

- `createListJWT(entry: StatusListEntity): Promise<void>` — Create status list tokens (JWT and CWT) and update the entity. The JWT includes: iat : When the token was issued (REQUIRED) exp : When the token expires (RECOMMENDED) ttl : How long verifiers can cache before fetching fresh copy (RECOMMENDED) aggregation\_uri : URI to fetch all status list URIs (OPTIONAL, per RFC Section 9)
- `createNewList(tenantId: string, options?: { credentialConfigurationId?: string; keyChainId?: string; bits?: BitsPerStatus; capacity?: number }): Promise<StatusListEntity>` — Create a new status list, optionally bound to a specific credential configuration and/or certificate.

- `findAvailableList(tenantId: string, credentialConfigurationId?: string): Promise<StatusListEntity | null>` — Find an available status list with free entries. Priority: dedicated list for the credential config \> shared lists
- `getEffectiveBits(tenantId: string): Promise<BitsPerStatus>` — Get the effective bits per status for a tenant.
- `getEffectiveCapacity(tenantId: string): Promise<number>` — Get the effective status list capacity for a tenant.
- `getListById(tenantId: string, listId: string): Promise<StatusListEntity>` — Get a specific status list by ID.
- `getListCwt(tenantId: string, listId: string): Promise<Uint8Array>` — Get the CWT for a specific status list. The CWT follows the same caching/freshness policy as JWT status list tokens.
- `getListJwt(tenantId: string, listId: string): Promise<string>` — Get the JWT for a specific status list.
- `getLists(tenantId: string): Promise<StatusListEntity[]>` — Get all status lists for a tenant.
- `getSigningCert(entry: StatusListEntity): unknown`
- `getStatusListUris(tenantId: string): Promise<string[]>` — Get all status list URIs for a tenant. Used for the status list aggregation endpoint (RFC Section 9.3).
- `hasStillFreeEntries(tenantId: string, credentialConfigurationId?: string): Promise<boolean>` — Check if there are still free entries available for a credential configuration.
- `importForTenant(tenantId: string): Promise<void>` — Import status list configurations for a specific tenant.
- `processStatusListConfig(tenantId: string, config: StatusListImportDto): any` — Process a status list config for import.
- `setEntry(listId: string, index: number, value: number, tenantId: string): Promise<void>` — Update the value of an entry in a specific status list. JWT regeneration depends on the tenant's immediateUpdate setting: If true: JWT is regenerated immediately If false (default): JWT is only regenerated on next request when TTL expires
- `shuffleArray(array: T[]): T[]` — Cryptographically secure Fisher-Yates shuffle
- `signStatusListCwt(tenantId: string, keyId: string, certChainPem: string[], payload: { subject: string; issuedAt: Date; expirationTime?: Date; ttl?: number; statusList: StatusList }): Promise<Uint8Array>`
- `updateList(tenantId: string, listId: string, updates: { credentialConfigurationId?: string | null; keyChainId?: string | null }): Promise<StatusListEntity>` — Update a status list's configuration (credential binding and/or certificate).
- `updateStatus(value: StatusUpdateDto, tenantId: string): Promise<void>` — Update the status of a session and its credential configuration.

### StatusListVerifierService

File: `src/trust/status-list-verifier.service.ts`

Description: Service for verifying status list entries. Fetches and caches status list JWTs, and checks the status of entries. See https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-status-list

Properties:
- `cache: unknown = new Map<string, CachedStatusList>()` — Cache of parsed status lists keyed by URI. Uses a simple in-memory cache with TTL support.
- `cachedJwts: unknown = new Map<string, CachedJwt>()` — Cache of raw status list JWTs keyed by URI. Used by statusListFetcher interface for SD-JWT SDK.
- `defaultCacheTtlMs: unknown = 5 * 60 * 1000` — Default cache TTL in milliseconds (5 minutes)
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(StatusListVerifierService.name)`

Methods:
- `checkStatus(statusListUri: string, index: number): Promise<StatusCheckResult>` — Check the status at a specific index in a status list.
- `checkStatusFromJwt(jwt: string): Promise<StatusCheckResult | undefined>` — Check the status of a JWT that contains a status claim. This will fetch the status list (with caching) and check the status at the specified index.
- `clearCache(uri?: string): void` — Clear the cache for a specific URI or all URIs.
- `fetchStatusListToken(uri: string, timeoutMs: number = 10000, type: "jwt" | "cwt" = "jwt"): Promise<string | Uint8Array>` — Fetch a status list JWT from a URI.
- `getCacheStats(): { size: number; jwtCacheSize: number; uris: string[] }` — Get cache statistics for monitoring.
- `getStatusDescription(status: StatusType): string` — Get a human-readable description for a status value.
- `getStatusEntryFromJwt(jwt: string): StatusListEntry | undefined` — Get the status entry from a JWT that contains a status claim. This extracts the status\_list reference (uri and idx) from the JWT.
- `getStatusList(uri: string): Promise<StatusList>` — Get a status list from cache or fetch it.
- `getStatusListJwt(uri: string): Promise<string>` — Get a status list JWT from cache or fetch it. This is useful when you need the raw JWT string (e.g., for SDK's statusListFetcher). The JWT is cached based on its TTL/exp claims.
- `isCacheExpired(cached: CachedStatusList): boolean` — Check if a cache entry is expired.
- `isJwtCacheExpired(cached: CachedJwt): boolean` — Check if a JWT cache entry is expired.
- `isTimedCacheExpired(cached: { fetchedAt: number; ttl?: number; exp?: number }): boolean` — Shared expiration logic for parsed-list and raw-token caches.

### WalletAttestationService

Properties:

The status claim is optional per the spec, so if not present, validation passes. Also verifies that the status list JWT is signed by the revocation certificate from the same trusted entity that issued the wallet attestation.

Validates the attestation JWT signature, checks the X.509 certificate chain against configured trust lists, and verifies the status list if present.

### X509ValidationService

File: `src/trust/x509-validation.service.ts`

Properties:
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(X509ValidationService.name)`

Methods:
- `buildPath(leaf: x509.X509Certificate, presentedChain: x509.X509Certificate[], anchors: x509.X509Certificate[], extraIntermediates: x509.X509Certificate[] = []): Promise<x509.X509Certificate[]>` — Build a validated path from leaf using provided chain + anchors. Returns path leaf..anchor if successful.
- `isCaCert(cert: x509.X509Certificate): boolean` — Determine whether anchor is a CA cert (basicConstraints CA=TRUE).
- `isTimeValid(cert: x509.X509Certificate, now: unknown = new Date()): boolean` — Basic time validity check (you may rely on chain builder already doing this, but keeping it explicit is sometimes useful).
- `parseTrustAnchors(values: Array<{ certValue: string }>): x509.X509Certificate[]`
- `parseX5c(x5c: X5cInput): x509.X509Certificate[]`
- `pathMatchesTrustedEntities(path: x509.X509Certificate[], entities: TrustedEntity[], pinnedMode: "leaf" | "pathEnd" = "leaf", serviceTypeFilter: string = "/Issuance"): Promise<MatchedTrustedEntity | null>` — Match a certificate chain against TrustedEntities. Returns the matched entity with its issuance and revocation certificates. Policy: Looks for certificates matching the specified service type in each entity If cert is CA: require path terminates in that anchor If cert is not CA: treat as pin pinnedMode "leaf": leaf equals pinned cert pinnedMode "pathEnd": path end equals pinned cert Example : (e.g., "/Issuance" matches both PID/Issuance and EAA/Issuance). Otherwise uses exact matching (e.g., full WalletProvider URI). Defaults to "/Issuance" to match both PID and EAA issuance.

### AddCredentialRequestEncryptionToIssuanceConfig1753100000000

File: `src/database/migrations/1753100000000-AddCredentialRequestEncryptionToIssuanceConfig.ts`

Description: Add credentialRequestEncryption column to issuance\_config table. This migration adds an optional boolean credentialRequestEncryption column so each issuance configuration can opt in to advertising credential\_request\_encryption in the credential issuer metadata, which publishes the issuer's encryption public key so wallets can send encrypted credential requests. It defaults to false because not all wallets support this feature.

Per OID4VP spec Section 13.3 (direct\_post response mode security): walletNonce: Separates wallet-facing identifier (request-id) from session ID (transaction-id) to prevent session fixation. responseCode: Generated after VP Token processing, included in redirect\_uri so only the legitimate frontend can confirm completion.

### AwsKmsAdapter

File: `src/crypto/key/kms/adapters/aws-kms.adapter.ts`

Description: AWS KMS adapter. Generates ECC\_NIST\_P256 SIGN\_VERIFY keys directly inside AWS KMS; private key material never leaves the HSM-backed service. Signing goes through the KMS Sign API and the returned DER ECDSA-Sig-Value is re-encoded as raw r \|\| s so it is JWS-compatible. Import of external key material is intentionally not supported.

Properties:
- `accessKeyId?: string`
- `capabilities: KmsAdapterCapabilities = { canCreate: true, canImport: false, canDelete: true, supportedAlgs: ["ES256"], defaultAlg: "ES256", }`
- `clientPromise?: Promise<KMSClient>`
- `jwkCache: unknown = new PublicJwkCache()`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(AwsKmsAdapter.name)`
- `providerId: string`
- `region: string`
- `secretAccessKey?: string`
- `type: KmsProviderType = "aws-kms"`

Methods:
- `assertSupported(alg: KmsSigningAlg): void`
- `client(): Promise<KMSClient>`
- `deleteKey(ref: KmsKeyRef): Promise<void>`
- `fetchPublicJwk(keyId: string, alg: KmsSigningAlg, kid: string): Promise<JWK>`
- `fetchPublicJwkFromKms(keyId: string, alg: KmsSigningAlg, kid: string): Promise<JWK>`
- `generateKey(opts: { kid: string; alg?: KmsSigningAlg }): Promise<KmsKeyMaterial>`
- `health(): Promise<KmsHealthResult>`
- `importKey(_opts: { kid: string; privateJwk: JWK; alg?: KmsSigningAlg }): Promise<KmsKeyMaterial>`
- `sign(ref: KmsKeyRef, data: Uint8Array, alg?: KmsSigningAlg): Promise<Uint8Array>`

### ChainedAsConfig

File: `src/issuer/configuration/issuance/dto/chained-as-config.dto.ts`
Extends: `createZodDto(ChainedAsConfigSchema)`

Description: Configuration for enabling "Chained Authorization Server" mode. In this mode, EUDIPLO acts as the Authorization Server for wallets, but delegates user authentication to an upstream OIDC provider (e.g., Keycloak). Benefits: No modifications required to the upstream OIDC provider EUDIPLO can include issuer\_state in access tokens for session correlation EUDIPLO handles wallet attestation and OID4VCI-specific requirements DPoP binding is managed by EUDIPLO Flow: Wallet receives credential offer with authorization\_server = EUDIPLO Wallet calls EUDIPLO PAR/authorize endpoints EUDIPLO redirects user to upstream OIDC provider for login User authenticates with upstream provider Upstream provider redirects back to EUDIPLO callback EUDIPLO exchanges upstream code for tokens, extracts user identity EUDIPLO issues its own access token with issuer\_state , DPoP binding, etc. Wallet uses EUDIPLO-issued token for credential requests

Properties:
- `enabled: boolean` — Whether chained AS mode is enabled. When enabled, EUDIPLO acts as the AS and delegates to upstream for authentication.
- `requireDPoP?: boolean` — Whether to require DPoP for token requests. When true, wallets must provide DPoP proofs. true
- `token?: ChainedAsTokenConfig` — Configuration for tokens issued by EUDIPLO.
- `upstream?: UpstreamOidcConfig` — Configuration for the upstream OIDC provider. Required when enabled is true.
- `vp?: ChainedAsVpConfig` — Configuration for a VP-backed AS facade.

### CredentialConfig

File: `src/issuer/configuration/credentials/entities/credential.entity.ts`

Properties:
- `attributeProvider?: AttributeProviderEntity`
- `attributeProviderId?: string | null` — Reference to the attribute provider used for fetching claims. Optional: if set, claims will be fetched from this provider during issuance.
- `config: IssuerMetadataCredentialConfig`
- `description?: string | null`
- `embeddedDisclosurePolicy?: EmbeddedDisclosurePolicy | null` — Embedded disclosure policy (discriminated union by policy ). The discriminator metadata is retained for OpenAPI schema generation.
- `fields: ClaimFieldDefinitionDto[]`
- `iaeActions?: IaeAction[] | null` — List of Interactive Authorization Endpoint (IAE) actions to execute before credential issuance. Actions are executed in order. Each action can be: openid4vp\_presentation : Request a verifiable presentation from the wallet redirect\_to\_web : Redirect user to a web page for additional interaction If empty or not set, no interactive authorization is required. Example : \[ { "type": "openid4vp\_presentation", "presentationConfigId": "pid-config" }, { "type": "redirect\_to\_web", "url": "https://example.com/verify", "label": "Additional Verification" } \]
- `id: string`
- `keyBinding?: boolean`
- `keyChain?: KeyChainEntity`
- `keyChainId?: string` — Reference to the key chain used for signing. Optional: if not specified, the default attestation key chain will be used.
- `lifeTime?: number`
- `schemaMeta?: SchemaMetaConfig | null` — TS11 schema metadata configuration for EUDI Catalogue of Attestations. When present, EUDIPLO can generate a SchemaMeta object per the TS11 spec using the GET /issuer/credentials/:id/schema-metadata endpoint. The underlying TS11 specification is not yet finalized.
- `sdJwtTrustFormat?: SdJwtTrustFormat | null` — For SD-JWT credentials: determines whether to include certificate chain (x5c) or use federation-based trust (iss claim). Default: "x5c" (federation must be explicitly selected)
- `statusManagement?: boolean`
- `tenant: TenantEntity` — The tenant that owns this object.
- `tenantId: string`
- `vct?: string | VCT | null`
- `webhookEndpoint?: WebhookEndpointEntity`
- `webhookEndpointId?: string | null` — Reference to the webhook endpoint used for notifications. Optional: if set, notifications will be sent to this endpoint.

### CredentialRequestException

File: `src/issuer/issuance/oid4vci/exceptions/credential-request.exception.ts`
Extends: `HttpException`

Description: Exception for OID4VCI Credential Request errors. According to the OID4VCI specification (Section 8.3.1.2), the response MUST use HTTP status code 400 and contain error and optionally error\_description . Error codes: invalid\_credential\_request : The Credential Request is missing a required parameter, includes an unsupported parameter or parameter value, repeats the same parameter, or is otherwise malformed. unknown\_credential\_configuration : Requested Credential Configuration is unknown. unknown\_credential\_identifier : Requested Credential identifier is unknown. invalid\_proof : The proofs parameter in the Credential Request is invalid: (1) if the field is missing, or (2) one of the provided key proofs is invalid, or (3) if at least one of the key proofs does not contain a c\_nonce value. invalid\_nonce : The proofs parameter in the Credential Request uses an invalid nonce. invalid\_encryption\_parameters : Encryption parameters are either invalid or missing when the Credential Issuer requires encrypted responses. credential\_request\_denied : The Credential Request has not been accepted. The Wallet SHOULD treat this error as unrecoverable.

### DbKmsAdapter

File: `src/crypto/key/kms/adapters/db-kms.adapter.ts`

Description: Database-backed KMS adapter. Key material is generated locally via WebCrypto and the private JWK is returned in KmsKeyRef.privateJwk so it can be persisted in the encrypted KeyChainEntity.activeJwk column. Signing imports the JWK on demand and calls crypto.subtle.sign . This adapter preserves the historical pre-abstraction behavior so existing tenants are unaffected by the KMS refactor.

Properties:
- `capabilities: KmsAdapterCapabilities = { canCreate: true, canImport: true, canDelete: true, supportedAlgs: ["ES256"], defaultAlg: "ES256", }`
- `type: KmsProviderType = "db"`

Methods:
- `assertSupported(alg: KmsSigningAlg): void`
- `deleteKey(_ref: KmsKeyRef): Promise<void>`
- `generateKey(opts: { kid: string; alg?: KmsSigningAlg }): Promise<KmsKeyMaterial>`
- `health(): Promise<KmsHealthResult>`
- `importKey(opts: { kid: string; privateJwk: JWK; alg?: KmsSigningAlg }): Promise<KmsKeyMaterial>`
- `sign(ref: KmsKeyRef, data: Uint8Array, alg?: KmsSigningAlg): Promise<Uint8Array>`

### DeferredCredentialException

File: `src/issuer/issuance/oid4vci/exceptions/deferred-credential.exception.ts`
Extends: `HttpException`

Description: Exception for OID4VCI Deferred Credential errors. According to the OID4VCI specification (Section 9.3), the response depends on the error type: issuance\_pending : HTTP 400 - The credential issuance is still pending. The response includes an optional interval field indicating the minimum amount of time in seconds the Wallet needs to wait before calling the Deferred Credential Endpoint again. invalid\_transaction\_id : HTTP 400 - The transaction\_id is invalid (e.g., not found, already used, or expired).

### HttpKmsAdapter

File: `src/crypto/key/kms/adapters/http-kms.adapter.ts`

Description: HTTP KMS adapter. Delegates all key-management operations to a remote microservice over HTTP/HTTPS. Private key material is never handled by the backend process — the remote service is solely responsible for storing and using it. Remote service API contract The microservice must implement the following endpoints: Method Path Description POST {keysPath} Generate a key POST {keysPath}/{kid}/sign Produce a signature DELETE {keysPath}/{kid} Delete a key GET {healthPath} Health check POST {keysPath}/{kid}/import Import a private JWK (optional) POST {keysPath} — generate key Request body: Example : { "kid": "my-key-id", "alg": "ES256" } Response (200): Example : { "publicJwk": { "kty": "EC", "crv": "P-256", ... } } POST {keysPath}/{kid}/sign — sign Request body: Example : { "data": "\<base64-encoded bytes\>", "alg": "ES256" } Response (200): Example : { "signature": "\<base64url-encoded raw r\|\|s\>" } DELETE {keysPath}/{kid} — delete Response: 204 No Content GET {healthPath} — health Response (200): Example : { "ok": true } POST {keysPath}/{kid}/import — import (optional) Request body: Example : { "privateJwk": { ... }, "alg": "ES256" } Response (200): Example : { "publicJwk": { "kty": "EC", "crv": "P-256", ... } } Return 404 or 405 if not supported.

Properties:
- `auth: HttpKmsAuth`
- `baseUrl: string`
- `capabilities: KmsAdapterCapabilities`
- `healthPath: string`
- `httpsAgent?: https.Agent` — Pre-built HTTPS agent for mTLS (undefined for other auth types).
- `jwkCache: unknown = new PublicJwkCache()`
- `keysPath: string`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(HttpKmsAdapter.name)`
- `oauth2TokenCache: literal type | null = null` — Cached OAuth 2.0 access token and its expiry timestamp.
- `providerId: string`
- `type: KmsProviderType = "http"`

Methods:
- `assertSupported(alg: KmsSigningAlg): void`
- `deleteKey(ref: KmsKeyRef): Promise<void>`
- `generateKey(opts: { kid: string; alg?: KmsSigningAlg }): Promise<KmsKeyMaterial>`
- `getOAuth2Token(): Promise<string>` — Returns a valid OAuth 2.0 access token, fetching a new one from the token endpoint when the cached token is absent or within 30 s of expiry.
- `health(): Promise<KmsHealthResult>`
- `importKey(opts: { kid: string; privateJwk: JWK; alg?: KmsSigningAlg }): Promise<KmsKeyMaterial>`
- `requestConfig(): Promise<{ headers: Record<string, string>; httpsAgent?: https.Agent }>` — Builds the Axios request config (headers + optional httpsAgent) for a request to the remote KMS service. none → no Authorization header bearer → static Authorization: Bearer \<token\> oauth2-client-credentials → fetches/caches a short-lived access token mtls → no Authorization header; the pre-built httpsAgent carries the client certificate
- `sign(ref: KmsKeyRef, data: Uint8Array, alg?: KmsSigningAlg): Promise<Uint8Array>`

### IssuanceConfig

File: `src/issuer/configuration/issuance/entities/issuance-config.entity.ts`

Description: Entity to manage issuance configs

Properties:
- `authorizationServers: ManagedAuthorizationServerConfig[]` — Dedicated managed authorization servers hosted by this issuer. Each entry creates a distinct AS endpoint and can be bound to a different presentation configuration.
- `batchSize?: number` — Value to determine the amount of credentials that are issued in a batch. Default is 1.
- `createdAt: Date` — The timestamp when the VP request was created.
- `credentialRequestEncryption?: boolean` — Whether to advertise credential\_request\_encryption in the credential issuer metadata. When enabled, the issuer publishes its encryption public key so wallets can send encrypted credential requests. Set encryption\_required to enforce it. Default: false
- `credentialResponseEncryption?: boolean` — Whether to advertise support for credential response encryption in the credential issuer metadata ( credential\_response\_encryption ). When enabled, wallets MAY request encrypted credential responses. Some wallets reject issuer metadata that advertises unsupported algorithms, so this defaults to false. Default: false
- `display: DisplayInfo[]`
- `dPopRequired?: boolean` — Indicates whether DPoP is required for the issuance process. Default value is true.
- `federation?: FederationConfig | null` — Optional OpenID Federation configuration used for trust evaluation. When omitted, trust checks rely on existing LoTE trust-list behavior.
- `registrationCertificate?: IssuerRegistrationCertificateConfig | null` — Optional registration certificate configuration for issuer metadata ( issuer\_info ). Supports importing an existing JWT or generating one via registrar.
- `registrationCertificateCache?: IssuerRegistrationCertificateCache | null` — Server-managed cache for generated issuer registration certificates.
- `signingKeyId?: string` — Optional key ID to use for signing access tokens. Must reference an existing key managed by the key service. If not set, the first available signing key for the tenant is used.
- `tenant: TenantEntity` — The tenant that owns this object.
- `tenantId: string` — Tenant ID for the issuance configuration.
- `txCodeMaxAttempts?: number` — Maximum number of failed tx\_code (transaction code) validation attempts before the pre-authorized code is invalidated. Protects against brute-force attacks on the OID4VCI pre-authorized code flow. Default: 5. Set to null to disable the limit (not recommended).
- `updatedAt: Date` — The timestamp when the VP request was last updated.
- `walletAttestationRequired?: boolean` — Indicates whether wallet attestation is required for the token endpoint. When enabled, wallets must provide OAuth-Client-Attestation headers. Default value is false.
- `walletProviderTrustLists?: WalletProviderTrustListRefDto[]` — Trust lists containing trusted wallet providers. Each entry MUST include either verifierKey or verifierX509Der .

### KmsCryptoProvider

File: `src/crypto/key/kms/kms-crypto-provider.ts`

Description: Crypto implementation that delegates to the native WebCrypto for everything except subtle.sign(...) invocations whose key was produced by makeKmsSigningKey. Those are routed to the appropriate KMS adapter. This is installed as the global @peculiar/x509 crypto provider so X509CertificateGenerator.create({ signingKey }) can be called with a fake KMS-backed key and the signature is produced inside the KMS backend — the private key never leaves it.

Properties:
- `native: Crypto = globalThis.crypto`
- `subtle: SubtleCrypto`

Methods:
- `getRandomValues(array: T): T`
- `randomUUID(): template literal type`
- `signDispatch(alg: AlgorithmIdentifier | RsaPssParams | EcdsaParams, key: CryptoKey, data: BufferSource): Promise<ArrayBuffer>`

### MigrateKeysToKeyChain1747000000000

File: `src/database/migrations/1747000000000-MigrateKeysToKeyChain.ts`

Description: Migration: Migrate legacy key\_entity + cert\_entity data to key\_chain table. This is a BREAKING CHANGE migration for the major release. The migration: Copies key data from key\_entity to key\_chain Joins the active certificate from cert\_entity Drops the legacy tables (key\_entity, cert\_entity, key\_usage\_entity, cert\_usage\_entity) Note: Keys with a signingCaKeyId (CA-signed) will have the CA embedded as rootKey/rootCertificate if the CA key exists. Otherwise, they become standalone self-signed keys.

### Pkcs11KmsAdapter

File: `src/crypto/key/kms/adapters/pkcs11-kms.adapter.ts`

Description: PKCS#11 KMS adapter. Generates ECDSA P-256 keys directly inside the HSM/token via the PKCS#11 interface and routes all signing through C\_Sign . Private key material is created with CKA\_SENSITIVE=true and CKA\_EXTRACTABLE=false so it never leaves the device. Keys are addressed by their PKCS#11 CKA\_LABEL , which we set to the caller-supplied kid . The label doubles as the externalKeyId on the resulting KmsKeyRef. The native module pkcs11js is loaded lazily on first use so deployments that don't configure a PKCS#11 provider don't need the library installed or the platform toolchain to build it.

Properties:
- `capabilities: KmsAdapterCapabilities = { canCreate: true, canImport: false, canDelete: true, supportedAlgs: ["ES256"], defaultAlg: "ES256", }`
- `config: Pkcs11AdapterConfig`
- `constants?: Pkcs11Constants`
- `initPromise?: Promise<void>`
- `jwkCache: unknown = new PublicJwkCache()`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(Pkcs11KmsAdapter.name)`
- `pkcs11?: Pkcs11Instance`
- `providerId: string`
- `session?: Buffer`
- `type: KmsProviderType = "pkcs11"`

Methods:
- `assertSupported(alg: KmsSigningAlg): void`
- `deleteKey(ref: KmsKeyRef): Promise<void>`
- `ensureSession(): Promise<{ p11: Pkcs11Instance; c: Pkcs11Constants; session: Buffer }>`
- `findObject(p11: Pkcs11Instance, c: Pkcs11Constants, session: Buffer, keyClass: number, label: string): Buffer | null`
- `generateKey(opts: { kid: string; alg?: KmsSigningAlg }): Promise<KmsKeyMaterial>`
- `health(): Promise<KmsHealthResult>`
- `importKey(_opts: { kid: string; privateJwk: JWK; alg?: KmsSigningAlg }): Promise<KmsKeyMaterial>`
- `initialise(): Promise<void>`
- `readPublicJwk(kid: string, alg: KmsSigningAlg, handle: Buffer): Promise<JWK>`
- `selectSlot(p11: Pkcs11Instance, slots: Buffer[]): Buffer`
- `sign(ref: KmsKeyRef, data: Uint8Array, alg?: KmsSigningAlg): Promise<Uint8Array>`
