### PublicJwkCache

File: `src/crypto/key/kms/public-jwk-cache.ts`

Description: Tiny TTL cache for public JWKs returned by external KMS providers. Public keys are immutable for the lifetime of a given external key id, but key rotation may rebind the same logical id to a new physical key — so we cap entries to a short TTL (default 5 minutes) rather than relying on explicit invalidation alone.

Properties:
- `entries: unknown = new Map< string, { jwk: JWK; expiresAt: number } >()`
- `ttlMs: number`

Methods:
- `clear(): void`
- `get(key: string): JWK | undefined`
- `invalidate(key: string): void`
- `set(key: string, jwk: JWK): void`

### RegistrarConfigResponseDto

    RegistrarConfigEntity,
    ["tenant", "tenantId", "password"] as const,

Description: DTO for the registrar configuration response. Excludes the password field for security and includes a flag indicating if a password is set.

### StatusListConfig

File: `src/auth/tenant/entities/status-list-config.ts`

Description: Configuration for status list behavior per tenant.

Properties:
- `bits?: BitsPerStatus` — The number of bits used per status entry. 1 bit: only valid/revoked states 2 bits: valid/revoked/suspended states 4 or 8 bits: extended status values If not set, uses the global STATUS\_BITS environment variable (default: 1).
- `capacity?: number` — The capacity of the status list (number of entries). If not set, uses the global STATUS\_CAPACITY environment variable (default: 10000).
- `enableAggregation?: boolean` — Whether to include the aggregation\_uri in status list JWTs. When enabled, each status list JWT will contain an aggregation\_uri claim pointing to an endpoint that returns all status list URIs for this tenant. This allows relying parties to pre-fetch all status lists for offline validation. See RFC draft-ietf-oauth-status-list Section 9.
- `immediateUpdate?: boolean` — If true, the JWT is regenerated immediately on every status change. If false (default), the JWT is only regenerated when requested and the TTL has expired. Use immediate mode for high-security scenarios where revocation must be visible instantly.
- `ttl?: number` — Time-to-live in seconds for the status list JWT. The JWT will include an exp claim enabling verifier caching. When the TTL expires, a new JWT is generated on the next request. If not set, uses the global STATUS\_TTL environment variable (default: 3600 = 1 hour).

### StatusListImportDto

File: `src/issuer/status-list/dto/status-list-import.dto.ts`

Description: DTO for importing a status list configuration from a JSON file. This enables "config as code" for status lists.

Properties:
- `bits?: BitsPerStatus` — Optional bits per status. If not provided, uses the tenant's configured default or the global default.
- `capacity?: number` — Optional capacity of the status list (number of entries). If not provided, uses the tenant's configured default or the global default.
- `credentialConfigurationId?: string | null` — Optional credential configuration ID to bind this list exclusively to. If not provided, the list will be shared and available for any credential configuration.
- `id: string` — Unique identifier for the status list. Used to check if the list already exists and for updates.
- `keyChainId?: string` — Optional key chain ID to use for signing this status list's JWT. If not provided, uses the tenant's default StatusList key chain.

### TokenErrorException

File: `src/issuer/issuance/oid4vci/exceptions/token-error.exception.ts`
Extends: `HttpException`

Description: Exception for OAuth 2.0 Token Error responses. According to RFC 6749 Section 5.2 and OID4VCI Section 6.3, the response MUST use HTTP status code 400 and contain error and optionally error\_description . Error codes from RFC 6749: invalid\_request : The request is missing a required parameter, includes an unsupported parameter value (other than grant type), repeats a parameter, includes multiple credentials, utilizes more than one mechanism for authenticating the client, or is otherwise malformed. invalid\_client : Client authentication failed (e.g., unknown client, no client authentication included, or unsupported authentication method). invalid\_grant : The provided authorization grant (e.g., authorization code, resource owner credentials) or refresh token is invalid, expired, revoked, does not match the redirection URI used in the authorization request, or was issued to another client. unauthorized\_client : The authenticated client is not authorized to use this authorization grant type. unsupported\_grant\_type : The authorization grant type is not supported by the authorization server. invalid\_scope : The requested scope is invalid, unknown, malformed, or exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner.

### TolerantIssuerAlternativeNameExtension

File: `src/shared/utils/x509-tolerant-extensions.ts`
Extends: `Extension`

Description: Tolerant replacement for @peculiar/x509's IssuerAlternativeNameExtension. Some real-world certificates carry a malformed issuerAltName: the extension value wraps a full nested Extension structure (OID 2.5.29.18 + OCTET STRING) around the GeneralNames instead of containing the GeneralNames directly. A prominent example is the EU Age Verification reference-implementation IACA/DS certificates ("Age Verification Issuer CA 01"). typed extension throws "Data does not match to GeneralName ASN1 schema" while parsing it — and because X509Certificate.extensions parses every extension, this breaks X509ChainBuilder and any cert.getExtension() call for such certificates, making their credentials unverifiable. This subclass parses the GeneralNames on a best-effort basis (unwrapping the nested-Extension variant when present) and falls back to the raw extension bytes instead of throwing.

Properties:
- `names?: GeneralNames`

Methods:
- `tryParseNames(bytes: ArrayBuffer): GeneralNames | undefined`

### TrustListUnavailableError

File: `src/verifier/presentations/credential/credential-chain-validation.service.ts`
Extends: `Error`

Description: Raised when a trust list WAS configured for a credential but could not be turned into a usable trust store — the fetch/parse/signature check failed, or the list is stale (its NextUpdate is in the past). This is deliberately distinct from "no trust list configured": the latter is a legitimate opt-out (trust validation is opt-in per credential), whereas this error means a requested security control is unavailable and verification MUST fail closed rather than silently accept the credential.

### VaultKmsAdapter

File: `src/crypto/key/kms/adapters/vault-kms.adapter.ts`

Description: HashiCorp Vault Transit KMS adapter. Keys are generated natively inside Vault and never leave the Transit engine. The adapter retrieves the public key for SubjectPublicKeyInfo / JWKS purposes and routes all signing operations through the Transit sign endpoint. Import is supported via Transit BYOK but requires Vault to be set up with a wrapping key (see Vault docs). Without that, callers should generate new keys directly in Vault.

Properties:
- `capabilities: KmsAdapterCapabilities = { canCreate: true, canImport: true, canDelete: true, supportedAlgs: ["ES256"], defaultAlg: "ES256", }`
- `jwkCache: unknown = new PublicJwkCache()`
- `logger: unknown = new Logger(VaultKmsAdapter.name)`
- `mountEnsured: unknown = false`
- `providerId: string`
- `transitMount: string`
- `type: KmsProviderType = "vault"`
- `vaultToken: string`
- `vaultUrl: string`

Methods:
- `assertSupported(alg: KmsSigningAlg): void`
- `authHeaders(): Record<string, string>`
- `deleteKey(ref: KmsKeyRef): Promise<void>`
- `ensureMount(): Promise<void>` — Ensure the configured transit mount exists. Idempotent. Subsequent calls are cheap no-ops once the mount has been verified.
- `fetchPublicJwk(keyName: string, alg: KmsSigningAlg): Promise<JWK>`
- `fetchPublicJwkFromVault(keyName: string, alg: KmsSigningAlg): Promise<JWK>`
- `generateKey(opts: { kid: string; alg?: KmsSigningAlg }): Promise<KmsKeyMaterial>`
- `health(): Promise<KmsHealthResult>`
- `importKey(opts: { kid: string; privateJwk: JWK; alg?: KmsSigningAlg }): Promise<KmsKeyMaterial>`
- `sign(ref: KmsKeyRef, data: Uint8Array, alg?: KmsSigningAlg): Promise<Uint8Array>`

### KmsAdapter

File: `src/crypto/key/kms/kms-adapter.ts`

Description: Provider-agnostic contract for key material operations. Implementations encapsulate the storage and signing backend (database, HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS, CSC, ...). For non- db providers the private key material MUST stay inside the backend — adapters never return private CryptoKey objects. Certificate construction routes its signing operations through a custom @peculiar/x509 crypto provider that calls back into KmsAdapter.sign.

Properties:
- `capabilities: KmsAdapterCapabilities` — Static capabilities of this adapter type.
- `providerId: string` — Configured provider id (matches id in kms.json ).
- `type: KmsProviderType` — Adapter type (matches type in kms.json ).

Methods:
- `deleteKey(ref: KmsKeyRef): Promise<void>` — Delete the key from the adapter's backing store. Adapters that cannot delete (e.g. AWS KMS in default config) MUST throw or no-op.
- `generateKey(opts: { kid: string; alg?: KmsSigningAlg }): Promise<KmsKeyMaterial>` — Generate fresh key material in the provider's backing store.
- `health(): Promise<KmsHealthResult>` — Liveness/readiness probe for the underlying backend. The default implementation (for db ) always succeeds; external providers should make a cheap remote call (e.g. Vault /sys/health , AWS KMS ListKeys with limit 1) and return a non-throwing result.
- `importKey(opts: { kid: string; privateJwk: JWK; alg?: KmsSigningAlg }): Promise<KmsKeyMaterial>` — Import a pre-existing private JWK into the adapter's backing store. Adapters that cannot accept external key material (e.g. AWS KMS in the default configuration) MUST throw.
- `sign(ref: KmsKeyRef, data: Uint8Array, alg?: KmsSigningAlg): Promise<Uint8Array>` — Produce a raw ECDSA signature over data using the key identified by ref . The returned value MUST be the raw r \|\| s concatenation expected by JOSE / COSE (64 bytes for P-256). For X.509 the caller re-encodes to ECDSA-Sig-Value DER.

### KmsAdapterCapabilities

File: `src/crypto/key/kms/kms-adapter.ts`

Description: Static capabilities of a KMS adapter implementation.

Properties:
- `canCreate: boolean`
- `canDelete: boolean`
- `canImport: boolean`
- `defaultAlg: KmsSigningAlg` — Default algorithm used when caller does not specify one.
- `supportedAlgs: KmsSigningAlg[]` — Algorithms the adapter can sign with.

### KmsHealthResult

File: `src/crypto/key/kms/kms-adapter.ts`

Properties:
- `error?: string`
- `latencyMs?: number`
- `ok: boolean`

### KmsKeyMaterial

File: `src/crypto/key/kms/kms-adapter.ts`

Description: Result of generating or importing key material. Adapters MUST NOT return private CryptoKey objects — cert signing is routed through KmsAdapter.sign via a custom @peculiar/x509 crypto provider.

Properties:
- `ref: KmsKeyRef`

### KmsKeyRef

File: `src/crypto/key/kms/kms-adapter.ts`

Description: Opaque reference to a key stored by a KMS provider. For the db provider: privateJwk is populated (key material lives in the DB column, encrypted at rest). For external providers ( vault , aws-kms , csc ): externalKeyId identifies the key inside the provider (e.g. Vault key name, AWS KMS key ID/ARN) and the private key never leaves the provider. A reference always carries the public JWK so JWKS / DID resolution and SubjectPublicKeyInfo construction can happen without a round-trip.

Properties:
- `alg: KmsSigningAlg`
- `externalKeyId?: string`
- `privateJwk?: JWK`
- `publicJwk: JWK`

### KmsSigningKeyMarker

File: `src/crypto/key/kms/kms-crypto-provider.ts`

Description: Marker properties spliced onto a fake CryptoKey so that KmsCryptoProvider can detect KMS-backed signing operations.

Properties:
- `__kmsAdapter: KmsAdapter`
- `__kmsAlg: KmsSigningAlg`
- `__kmsRef: KmsKeyRef`

### OidcDiscoveryDto

File: `src/auth/dto/oidc-discovery.dto.ts`

Description: Data Transfer Object for OIDC Discovery Response. Based on OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 specification.

Properties:
- `acr_values_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the Authentication Context Class References that this OP supports.
- `authorization_endpoint?: string` — URL of the OP's OAuth 2.0 Authorization Endpoint.
- `claim_types_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the Claim Types that the OpenID Provider supports.
- `claims_locales_supported?: string[]` — Languages and scripts supported for values in Claims being returned.
- `claims_parameter_supported?: boolean` — Boolean value specifying whether the OP supports use of the claims parameter.
- `claims_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the Claim Names of the Claims that the OpenID Provider MAY be able to supply values for.
- `display_values_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the display parameter values that the OpenID Provider supports.
- `grant_types_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the OAuth 2.0 Grant Type values that this OP supports.
- `id_token_encryption_alg_values_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the JWE encryption algorithms supported by the OP for the ID Token.
- `id_token_encryption_enc_values_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the JWE encryption methods supported by the OP for the ID Token.
- `id_token_signing_alg_values_supported: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the JWS signing algorithms supported by the OP for the ID Token.
- `issuer: string` — URL using the https scheme with no query or fragment component that the OP asserts as its Issuer Identifier.
- `jwks_uri: string` — URL of the OP's JSON Web Key Set document.
- `op_policy_uri?: string` — URL that the OpenID Provider provides to the person registering the Client to read about the OP's requirements on how the Relying Party can use the data provided by the OP.
- `op_tos_uri?: string` — URL that the OpenID Provider provides to the person registering the Client to read about OpenID Provider's terms of service.
- `registration_endpoint?: string` — URL of the OP's Dynamic Client Registration Endpoint.
- `request_object_encryption_alg_values_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the JWE encryption algorithms supported by the OP for Request Objects.
- `request_object_encryption_enc_values_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the JWE encryption methods supported by the OP for Request Objects.
- `request_object_signing_alg_values_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the JWS signing algorithms supported by the OP for Request Objects.
- `request_parameter_supported?: boolean` — Boolean value specifying whether the OP supports use of the request parameter.
- `request_uri_parameter_supported?: boolean` — Boolean value specifying whether the OP supports use of the request\_uri parameter.
- `require_request_uri_registration?: boolean` — Boolean value specifying whether the OP requires any request\_uri values used to be pre-registered.
- `response_modes_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the OAuth 2.0 response\_mode values that this OP supports.
- `response_types_supported: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the OAuth 2.0 response\_type values that this OP supports.
- `scopes_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the OAuth 2.0 scope values that this server supports.
- `service_documentation?: string` — URL of a page containing human-readable information that developers might want or need to know when using the OpenID Provider.
- `subject_types_supported: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the Subject Identifier types that this OP supports.
- `token_endpoint: string` — URL of the OP's OAuth 2.0 Token Endpoint.
- `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of Client Authentication methods supported by this Token Endpoint.
- `token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the JWS signing algorithms supported by the Token Endpoint for the signature on the JWT used to authenticate the Client at the Token Endpoint for the private\_key\_jwt and client\_secret\_jwt authentication methods.
- `ui_client_id?: string` — Public client ID for the Angular UI (Authorization Code + PKCE). Only present in OIDC mode.
- `ui_locales_supported?: string[]` — Languages and scripts supported for the user interface.
- `userinfo_encryption_alg_values_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the JWE encryption algorithms supported by the OP for UserInfo Responses.
- `userinfo_encryption_enc_values_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the JWE encryption methods supported by the OP for UserInfo Responses.
- `userinfo_endpoint?: string` — URL of the OP's UserInfo Endpoint.
- `userinfo_signing_alg_values_supported?: string[]` — JSON array containing a list of the JWS signing algorithms supported by the OP for UserInfo Responses.

### WebhookResponse

File: `src/webhook/webhook.service.ts`

Description: Response from a webhook to receive credentials. Can include claims data for immediate issuance or a deferred flag for deferred issuance.

Properties:

- `redirectUri?: string` — Redirect URI for OAuth-style redirects.

- `applyTrustedAuthoritiesPolicy(dcqlQuery: T, removeTrustedAuthorities: boolean): T` — Conditionally strips trusted\_authorities from each credential query in a DCQL query object. Some wallets do not yet correctly handle trusted\_authorities in the DCQL query of an OID4VP authorization request. removeTrustedAuthorities is an escape hatch (controlled by the VP\_REMOVE\_TA env flag) for deployments that need to work around such wallets; it is disabled by default so trusted\_authorities is sent to wallets as configured.
  Defined in `src/verifier/oid4vp/dcql-trusted-authorities.util.ts`

  Defined in `src/verifier/iso18013/cbor-request.ts`
- `buildIsoMdocDcApiTranscript(encryptionInfoB64u: string, origin: string): Promise<{ hpkeInfo: Buffer; sessionTranscript: SessionTranscript }>` — Build the DCAPIHandover SessionTranscript per ISO/IEC TS 18013-7:2025 Annex C: SessionTranscript = \[null, null, \["dcapi", SHA-256(CBOR(\[encInfoB64u, origin\]))\]\] The transcript is used in two places: hpkeInfo : plain CBOR encoding — the HPKE RFC 9180 info parameter used by the wallet when encrypting and by the verifier when decrypting. sessionTranscript : the structure passed to Verifier.verifyDeviceResponse for DeviceAuth verification.
  Defined in `src/verifier/iso18013/cbor-request.ts`
- `buildItemsRequest(docType: string, namespaces: Record): ItemsRequest` — Build the ItemsRequest for a single mDOC docType per ISO 18013-5 §8.3.2.1.2.1. The same ItemsRequest instance must be embedded in both the DocRequest and the ReaderAuthentication structure so the wallet can recompute and verify the reader signature — see buildReaderAuth.
  Defined in `src/verifier/iso18013/cbor-request.ts`

- `buildP256Spki(x: Buffer, y: Buffer): Buffer` — Build a P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo around the raw uncompressed EC point so we can hand it to WebCrypto's SPKI importer. Layout (DER): SEQUENCE { AlgorithmIdentifier, BIT STRING { 04 \|\| x \|\| y } } where AlgorithmIdentifier = SEQUENCE { id-ecPublicKey, prime256v1 OID }.
  Defined in `src/crypto/key/kms/adapters/pkcs11-kms.adapter.ts`
- `buildPostgresSslOptions(readValue): boolean | TlsOptions` — Build PostgreSQL SSL settings from environment/config values. Supported variables: DB\_SSL=true\|false DB\_SSL\_REJECT\_UNAUTHORIZED=true\|false DB\_SSL\_CA\_PATH=/path/to/ca.crt DB\_SSL\_CERT\_PATH=/path/to/client.crt DB\_SSL\_KEY\_PATH=/path/to/client.key DB\_SSL\_KEY\_PASSPHRASE=secret
  Defined in `src/database/postgres-ssl-options.ts`
- `buildReaderAuth(itemsRequest: ItemsRequest, sessionTranscript: SessionTranscript, signingJwk: Record, certificateChain): Promise<ReaderAuth>` — Sign a detached ReaderAuth (COSE\_Sign1) authenticating the verifier inside the DeviceRequest, per ISO/IEC 18013-5 §9.1.4 / 18013-7 Annex C. The signed payload is the CBOR of ReaderAuthentication = \["ReaderAuthentication", SessionTranscript, ItemsRequestBytes\] carried as the COSE\_Sign1 detached payload ( ReaderAuthenticationBytes , a Tag-24-wrapped bstr). The verifier's certificate chain is placed in the unprotected x5chain header and ES256 in the protected header — the same shape @owf/mdoc produces for IssuerAuth, and the exact bytes its ReaderAuth.verify() recomputes. The DCAPIHandover SessionTranscript is available already at offer time (it is a deterministic function of encryptionInfo + browser origin), so the reader signature can be produced when the DeviceRequest is built.
  Defined in `src/verifier/iso18013/cbor-request.ts`

- `type TokenErrorCode = "invalid_request" | "invalid_client" | "invalid_grant" | "unauthorized_client" | "unsupported_grant_type" | "invalid_scope" | "invalid_tx_code"` — OAuth 2.0 Token Error Codes as defined in: RFC 6749 Section 5.2 ( https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6749#section-5.2 ) OID4VCI Section 6.3 ( https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-credential-issuance-1\_0.html#name-token-error-response ) OID4VCI specific clarifications: invalid\_request : The Authorization Server does not expect a Transaction Code in the Pre-Authorized Code Flow but the Client provides one. The Authorization Server expects a Transaction Code in the Pre-Authorized Code Flow but the Client does not provide one. invalid\_grant : The End-User provides the wrong Pre-Authorized Code or the Pre-Authorized Code has expired. invalid\_tx\_code : The Authorization Server expects a Transaction Code in the Pre-Authorized Code Flow but the Client provides the wrong Transaction Code. invalid\_client : The Client tried to send a Token Request with a Pre-Authorized Code without a Client ID but the Authorization Server does not support anonymous access.
- `type TrustAuthorityBase = Omit<TrustAuthority | schemaMetadata>`
- `type TrustedAuthorityInput = NonNullable`
- `type TrustedAuthorityQueryValue = TrustedAuthorityQueryEtsiTl | TrustedAuthorityQueryOpenIdFederation`
- `type TrustedEntity = { entityId?: string; services: TrustedEntityServiceCert[] }` — A TrustedEntity from a LoTE, containing its services grouped together. This preserves the relationship between issuance and revocation certificates from the same entity.
- `type TrustedEntityServiceCert = { serviceTypeIdentifier: ServiceTypeIdentifier; certValue: string }`
- `type TrustListEntity = InternalTrustListEntity | ExternalTrustListEntity`
- `type TrustListSource = { lotes: TrustListRef[]; acceptedServiceTypes?: ServiceTypeIdentifier[] }`
- `type TypedCredentialConfig = SdJwtDcCredentialConfig | MsoMdocCredentialConfig` — Union of the credential configs we actively support
- `type UpdateAttributeProvider = z.infer<typeof UpdateAttributeProviderSchema>`
- `type UpdateClient = z.infer<typeof UpdateClientSchema>`
- `type UpdateRegistrarConfig = z.infer<typeof UpdateRegistrarConfigSchema>`
- `type UpdateTenant = z.infer<typeof UpdateTenantSchema>`
- `type UpdateUser = z.infer<typeof UpdateUserSchema>`
- `type UpdateWebhookEndpoint = z.infer<typeof UpdateWebhookEndpointSchema>`
- `type Verifier = function`
- `type VerifierOptions = { trustListSource?: TrustListSource; federationTrustSource?: FederationTrustSource; policy: VerifyPolicy; transactionData?: string[]; keyBindingAudience?: strin…`
- `type VerifyPolicy = { requireX5c: boolean; revocation?: { enabled: boolean; failClosed?: boolean; fetchTimeoutMs?: number; cacheTtlMs?: number }; pinnedCertMode?: "leaf" | "pathEnd…`
- `type VocabularyStatus = typeof VOCABULARY_STATUS_VALUES['number']`
- `type X5cInput = string[]`
- `type ZodIssueLike = { path: ReadonlyArray<PropertyKey>; message: string; code: string }`

## Public enumerations

- `enum AttestationLoS` — Attestation Level of Security (LoS) as defined in TS11.
  - `HIGH = iso_18045_high`
  - `MODERATE = iso_18045_moderate`
  - `ENHANCED_BASIC = iso_18045_enhanced-basic`
  - `BASIC = iso_18045_basic`

- `enum AuthConfig` — Enum for the type of authentication used in webhooks.
  - `API_KEY = apiKey`
  - `NONE = none`

- `enum ChainedAsSessionStatus` — Status of a Chained AS session.
  - `PENDING_AUTHORIZE = pending_authorize`
  - `PENDING_UPSTREAM_CALLBACK = pending_upstream_callback`
  - `PENDING_VP_CALLBACK = pending_vp_callback`
  - `AUTHORIZED = authorized`
  - `TOKEN_ISSUED = token_issued`
  - `EXPIRED = expired`

- `enum CredentialFormat`
  - `MSO_MDOC = mso_mdoc`
  - `SD_JWT_VC = dc+sd-jwt`

- `enum CredentialProofType`
  - `JWT = jwt`
  - `ATTESTATION = attestation`

- `enum DeferredTransactionStatus` — Status of a deferred credential transaction.
  - `Pending = pending`
  - `Ready = ready`
  - `Retrieved = retrieved`
  - `Expired = expired`
  - `Failed = failed`

- `enum FederationEntityRole`
  - `TRUST_ANCHOR = trust_anchor`
  - `INTERMEDIATE = intermediate`
  - `LEAF = leaf`

- `enum FederationTrustMode`
  - `FEDERATION_ONLY = federation-only`
  - `HYBRID = hybrid`

- `enum IaeActionType` — Discriminator for IAE action types.
  - `OPENID4VP_PRESENTATION = openid4vp_presentation`
  - `REDIRECT_TO_WEB = redirect_to_web`

- `enum ImportPhase` — Import phase definitions with their order. Lower numbers run first.
  - `CORE = 10`
  - `CONFIGURATION = 20`
  - `REFERENCES = 30`
  - `FINAL = 40`

- `enum InteractionType` — Interaction type enum.
  - `OPENID4VP_PRESENTATION = openid4vp_presentation`
  - `REDIRECT_TO_WEB = redirect_to_web`

- `enum InteractiveAuthorizationRequestType` — Request type enum for internal use.
  - `INITIAL = initial`
  - `FOLLOW_UP = follow_up`

- `enum InteractiveAuthSessionStatus` — Status of an interactive authorization session.
  - `Pending = pending`
  - `AllStepsCompleted = all_steps_completed`

- `enum IssuerRegistrationCertificateMode`
  - `IMPORT = import`
  - `GENERATE = generate`

- `enum KeyChainType` — Key chain type determines the structure of the key chain.
  - `Standalone = standalone`
  - `InternalChain = internalChain`

- `enum KeyUsage` — Key usage types for cryptographic operations.
  - `Sign = sign`
  - `Encrypt = encrypt`

- `enum KeyUsageType` — Key usage types for different purposes in the system.
  - `Access = access`
  - `Attestation = attestation`
  - `TrustList = trustList`
  - `StatusList = statusList`
  - `Encrypt = encrypt`

- `enum MediaType` — Represents the media types used in the application.
  - `APPLICATION_JSON = application/json`
  - `APPLICATION_JWT = application/jwt`

- `enum RevocationCheckMode`
  - `Strict = strict`
  - `BestEffort = best_effort`
  - `Disabled = disabled`

- `enum Role` — Enumeration of all roles available in the system.
  - `Presentations = presentation:manage`
  - `PresentationRequest = presentation:request`
  - `Issuances = issuance:manage`
  - `IssuanceOffer = issuance:offer`
  - `Clients = clients:manage`
  - `Users = users:manage`
  - `Tenants = tenants:manage`
  - `Registrar = registrar:manage`

- `enum SchemaMetaBindingType` — Cryptographic binding type as defined in TS11.
  - `CLAIM = claim`
  - `KEY = key`
  - `BIOMETRIC = biometric`
  - `NONE = none`

- `enum SchemaMetadataPinMode`
  - `KEEP_CURRENT = keep_current`
  - `UPDATE_TO_NEW_VERSION = update_to_new_version`
  - `REPLACE_ID = replace_id`

- `enum SchemaMetaFrameworkType` — Trust framework type for trusted authorities.
  - `AKI = aki`
  - `ETSI_TL = etsi_tl`
  - `OPENID_FEDERATION = openid_federation`

- `enum SdJwtTrustFormat` — Determines how SD-JWT credentials are signed and trust is established. "x5c": Include certificate chain in JWT header (certificate-based trust) "federation": Include issuer entity ID in 'iss' claim (federation-based trust) "auto": Legacy mode kept for backward compatibility (treated like x5c)
  - `X5C = x5c`
  - `FEDERATION = federation`

- `enum ServiceTypeIdentifier`
  - `PIDIssuance = http://uri.etsi.org/19602/SvcType/PID/Issuance`
  - `EaaIssuance = http://uri.etsi.org/19602/SvcType/EAA/Issuance`
  - `EaaRevocation = http://uri.etsi.org/19602/SvcType/EAA/Revocation`

- `enum SessionCleanupMode` — Cleanup mode when sessions expire.
  - `Full = full`
  - `Anonymize = anonymize`

- `enum SessionStatus`
  - `Active = active`
  - `Fetched = fetched`
  - `Completed = completed`
  - `Expired = expired`
  - `Failed = failed`

- `enum TrustedAuthorityType`
  - `ETSI_TL = etsi_tl`
  - `OPENID_FEDERATION = openid_federation`
